statement_to_voters:
Since 2015 I've fought tooth and nail for our steelworks, successfully campaigned to keep Junction 41 open, and persuaded the UK government to scrap plans to build a prison in Baglan.

My team and I have resolved over 13,500 individual constituent cases, from housing to law & order issues, and I've held eight annual funding fairs that have helped 800 people representing 250 community groups. I also campaigned for the winning Celtic Freeport bid that will create thousands of well-paid jobs in our area by putting Port Talbot at the heart of the floating off-shore wind revolution.

If you put your trust in me I will continue to be an active local campaigner, and a strong national voice for Aberafan Maesteg.

In 2015, Kirsty Blackman became the UK Parliament member for the Aberdeen North Constituency having been elected to parliament with an impressive 56.4% of the vote.  Kirsty was re-elected in 2017 and again in 2019, this time with the biggest percentage majority in Scotland.Kirsty has held a number of front-bench roles for the SNP, and was the first woman ever to lead on the Economy in the House of Commons.  She was the Depute Leader of the SNP Westminster Group from 2017-2020.  She has spoken 1860 times in Parliament.Kirsty and her team have helped folk in Aberdeen North with over 30,000 problems, tackling nearly 70 new issues a week.  She has spent a lot of time working with and supporting local charities to best provide help and improve lives in our city.She has campaigned for a fairer Social Security System, a fairer immigration system and for changes to the energy markets to tackle rising costs and reduce inequalities which mean those in energy rich Scotland pay more for power than those in England or Wales.  Kirsty wants us all to live in a fairer, more equal Scotland and intends to continue working every day to make this happen.

I am proud to have been selected as the Labour Party’s candidate for Altrincham & Sale West for the upcoming general election.

This is our chance to offer hope for the future, and end 14 years of Tory chaos 

Vote for change on the 4th of July

Britain's had a Conservative government for 14 years. Throughout that time we've had a Conservative MP in Amber Valley. The country is now crying out for change and with your help, I'll be part of a Labour government which delivers it.



I'm Linsey Farnsworth, Labour's parliamentary candidate for Amber Valley. Amber Valley is my home and I live here with my husband and teenage children. I'm not a career politician, so for me, the opportunity to become the MP for Amber Valley is about serving my community and helping the people within it. That's why I became a Borough Councillor representing the people in my own ward: Kilburn, Denby, Holbrook and Horsley.



I was a Crown Prosecutor for 21 years until recently stepping back to concentrate on Amber Valley. I've watched the Conservatives govern as if it were a game, and I know many people in Amber Valley are feeling disillusioned with politics and politicians. I firmly believe we need to bring decency back into politics. In the Crown Prosecution Service I served with openness, honesty and fairness and treated everyone with respect. I've since been appointed as the Chair of Standards in Amber Valley Borough Council, in charge of ensuring Councillors stick to the code of conduct and step in if they don't.



I'm proud of my working class background. Growing up my dad was a coal miner and when the pits closed he was out of work. Money was tight and so I know how it is for people in Amber Valley, struggling under the cost-of-living crisis of this Conservative government's making. Under a Labour government my dad was able to retrain as a bricklayer and get our family back on its feet. As part of the next Labour government I'll work hard to support people through this cost-of-living crisis.



My mum died of cancer in 1989, diagnosed too late because our NHS was overburdened under a Conservative government. My step-mum is a nurse and my dad, who has dementia, was in hospital recently. I've witnessed first hand the strain our NHS is under again. In Amber Valley people are struggling to get appointments to see their GP or accessing an NHS dentist. As our MP I'll make it a priority to change this and to get our NHS back on its feet.



As a Crown Prosecutor I worked to bring criminals to justice and helped to give victims a voice in court. Most recently I worked internationally in British Embassies tackling serious criminals including people smugglers, fraudsters and drug gangs. With this background I'll focus on making us safer, whether that's nationally, working in government to take down the people smuggling gangs bringing vulnerable people into the country on small boats, or locally, working with our Police and Crime Commissioner Nicolle Ndiweni to put more police on the streets to tackle crime and anti-social behaviour in our town centres.



As a mother of teenage children I'm keen to be part of a Labour government which will prioritise their education, to make sure they all have a chance to fulfil their potential and that will tackle the climate crisis so that there is a future for them to look forward to.



If you elect me as our next MP you have my word that I'll be a strong voice in Parliament for Amber Valley, I'll serve with integrity and work hard every day for our community.

Brendan has served as the Member of Parliament for Argyll and Bute in 2015 and was until the General Election was called, the Scottish National Party’s spokesperson for Foreign Affairs at Westminster and was a member of the House of Commons’ Foreign Affairs Select Committee.  Prior to that he was party’s Chief Whip at Westminster having previously been the SNP spokesperson on both Defence and on Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.Before becoming an MP, he worked for almost two decades as television producer/director and worked for STV, SKY SPORTS and the BBC, before setting up his own independent television production company.Although Brendan and his family have lived in Argyll & Bute for more than 20 years, he was born in the east-end Glasgow and attended St. Andrew’s Secondary School in Carntyne. After school he worked in Glasgow District Council’s Housing Department before enrolling at the University of Strathclyde University from where he graduated with an honours degree in Economic and Social History and Modern History.

I was first elected as the MP for Arundel & South Downs in 2019 and live just outside Petworth with my family. I am not a ‘career politician’ and was only elected after 27 years in business, most of which was as a finance director of a FTSE100 company.

I am standing as your Conservative candidate at this election to keep on fighting for residents against unsustainable development, deliver safer and quieter roads, protect our nature, rivers and farmers and support our High Streets. Our rural schools, police and healthcare need the resources of a strong economy and an MP that understands the countryside.  I was honoured to have been elected your MP in 2019 and since then I have worked diligently and with integrity for all residents.

I believe in what Conservatives have always believed in: strong defence, firm action on crime, securing our borders, personal freedom, protecting pensioners’ incomes and being on the side of families who work hard through lower taxes. 

I’ve spent most of my life outside of politics, so I understand many people’s frustrations about Westminster. But we do need a strong local voice which is why I’m asking for your support at this election.

I moved to Ashford in 2002 and have been living here with my wife and three children ever since, taking great pride in calling Ashford my home. I am a mental health nurse, who has worked in the NHS for the past 22 years, and is currently working as Head of Nursing, Quality and Patient Safety. I started my NHS career at the Arundel unit based in the William Harvey Hospital as a junior nurse. I have been able to undertake many academic qualifications whilst working in the frontline, the highest being a master's degree in Health Care Leadership.

My lived experiences in the NHS, interactions with the patients and families as well as educational opportunities have all contributed to developing a greater insight into the issues that matter most to the people. Consequently, a desire to develop practical solutions with collaboration and innovation has led me to this current political candidacy.

I am currently a borough councillor, representing Aylesford and East Stour Ward. I believe that the MP for Ashford should be visible and stand up for the community. Someone who should address the problems that matter to the people of Ashford such as improved access to GP, Dental and hospital services, pothole-free roads, revitalising the town centre and bringing back Ashford International.

I am a hardworking, motivated and resilient individual who goes above and beyond to achieve the goal that is set with a purpose, be it in my personal, professional or public life. I am determined to make changes that bring efficiency in public services.

Getting elected to serve the people of Ashton-under-Lyne in 2015 was the honour of my life. I made a commitment to always do my utmost to get the very best for the people that I so proud and privileged to represent. I would love to continue doing so. This General Election gives you a choice - the chance to change Britain. After 14 years of the Conservatives, it's time for change. It's time for Labour.

Laura Kyrke-Smith is Labour's Parliamentary Candidate in Aylesbury. She is a charity leader and campaigner by background and she lives in Bucks with her husband and three children. Please do get in touch if you'd like to find out more about her campaign.

My Mum grew up on Merton Street and I live in the ward because I love it here. I love its diversity, history and heritage.

Our Community came together during the pandemic, with lots of examples of people helping their neighbours. From the Community Fridge to litter-picking, Grimsbury and Hightown is a community that cares.

As your Councillor I will fight for safer streets and cleaner estates.

I will push for more decent, affordable homes and better conditions for tenants.

I’ll stand up for all residents in Grimsbury and Hightown and would love to have your support on 4th May.

Our priorities for Cherwell

1. Deliver more genuinely affordable homes, to rent and to buy, for local people.

2. Tackle the 50% of homes in Cherwell that have an energy efficiency rating of below average.

3. Improve standards in rented accommodation with a Tenants’ Charter.

4. Action to address the climate emergency including a Citizens’ Assembly.

5. Put mental health and tackling loneliness at the heart of what the Council does.

6. Focus investment into creating dynamic town centres.

7. Clean up our estates with zero-tolerance to fly-tipping.

I’m Nesil Caliskan, your Labour candidate for Barking in the upcoming General Election on 4th July.

As a Labour Party member for 20 years and councillor since 2015 — I am an experienced campaigner, and know how to fight the Tories and win. In 2018 I was elected my borough’s first woman leader of the Council.

Since then, I’ve led a council that is on local people’s side — fighting against Tory cuts, delivering high-quality public services that support the most vulnerable, and working hard to deliver real life chances to everyone in the borough.

I’m asking for your support in this election to move on from the disastrous failure of the last 14 years under the Conservatives.

I’m here to work with local people to get things done. I’ll fight for good quality, affordable homes so young people and local families can get on the property ladder here in Barking. I’ll deliver more police, working with local businesses and our community.

Should I be lucky enough to earn your trust and vote as Barking’s Member of Parliament, I’ll be on your side, fight your corner and deliver for Barking.

Born and raised in Furness, with an in-depth understanding of the challenges and possibilities for our unique peninsula.

I'm standing because Furness deserves much more. Furness deserves an MP who cares and understands the needs of its locals, its businesses, and its infrastructure. Living here all my life, dedicating three decades to serving the community has given me a good insight into those needs. I'm committed to working hard and being honest about where I stand, prioritising residents and their concerns.

Fourteen years of Conservative government have brought huge cuts in funding to Barrow and Furness, leaving communities and town centres hollowed out and left behind, with an ever expanding gap of inequality. They now offer a small fraction of what should have been delivered over those years with "levelling up", forcing communities to battle each other for funds.

My drive in life is Community. I believe it's the bedrock of a lot of the best things in life and when we work together, we can achieve incredible things.

I've found that the links between my many roles, businesses, levels of government and community groups is the key to producing results. With a Labour MP and Labour government we can deliver. If elected, I will work to deliver the enormous potential we have here in Furness.

Why I'm running to be Basingstoke's first Labour MP After fourteen years of Conservative failure, political chaos and underachievement nationally on the economy and public services, and two decades of Maria Miller locally, it’s time for change.

Basingstoke is a fantastic town, and the UK a brilliant country, and Labour is ambitious for the future, but right now we’re being held back by a local MP who can’t deliver on her promises and a Government which has run out of ideas, is dominated by internal division, and is running out of road. It doesn’t have to be this way.

I will work so that Basingstoke, and everyone who lives here, is able to fulfil their full potential. Labour will restore Britain’s pride and purpose and move on from the division and chaos of the Tory years.

Wera Hobhouse lives with her husband William in Bath. They have four grown-up children.

Wera was first elected to Parliament in 2017. She has been instrumental in tackling violence against women and girls, making upskirting a criminal offence in England and Wales and enshrining the prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace into law in 2023.

As the Liberal Democrat spokesperson for Climate Change she is campaigning for a massive national roll-out of home insulation, advocates for 90% of our electricity to be generated from renewables by 2030 and for a roof top solar revolution.

In Bath, Wera has brought a police station back into the city. Social housing is being built in Bath for the first time in decades. HGV’s above 18 tonnes can no longer drive over Cleveland Bridge.

Wera’s voice in Parliament has a national impact.

There has never been a greater need for a Labour government. The cost of living crisis, compounded by years of Tory austerity and the devastating impacts of the pandemic, have resulted in an increasing number of people being pushed into poverty with many more struggling to get by.



I live in Bathgate where my husband and I have raised our family, with our three children attending local schools. Like most people, we depend on our NHS services including St John's Hospital and our local medical centre. The environment, transport and local services are all things that matter to me and my family in our everyday lives.



Since 2017, I've served as a Labour councillor for the Whitburn and Blackburn ward and as Depute Leader of West Lothian Council. I am passionate about fairness and social justice and have put these values front and centre of my work in local communities. Council budgets have seen real-term cuts from the SNP government over a number of years and front line services are struggling. It just doesn't have to be this way.



The people of Bathgate and Linlithgow, and the electorate across the UK, can choose a different future, with a UK Labour government and elected representatives that will put their needs first, ending the years of chaos and division we've seen under both the Tories and the SNP.



We need a fresh start. Join our campaign and help deliver the change we need.

I live in Beckenham and Penge, and I'm standing to be the first Labour MP for our new constituency. I have fought and won successful campaigns for our local communities already, including saving train station ticket offices last summer. Throughout my professional career, working in education and for a tech start-up, I've made a difference and got things done.

I've also campaigned for over a decade for disabled people and their families. When I was 13, an accident left me unable to walk for four years. I went back a year at school, and at 17 I became one of the youngest people in Britain to have a hip replacement. I've never forgotten the care and compassion I received from NHS staff, I owe them everything. They inspired me to fight for others, just like they fought for me.

14 years of Conservative chaos, division and failure has left working people paying the price with soaring mortgages and bills. They have stripped kindness and humanity from the heart of government. I'm standing because I believe change is possible, and I want to bring my campaigning experience to be a strong voice for our area.

Most of our new constituency has had Tory MPs for over 80 years. If you agree it's time for change, I'm asking you to lend me your vote at this election.

In 2019, with the hard work of volunteers, we held Bedford and Kempston by a majority of just 145 votes. The next election will be vital to form the Labour Government we all need and continuing to hold Bedford and Kempston is a vital part of that.

We rely on donations big and small from people across the country to help keep Bedford red. If you can afford to contribute, please do so using the button at the bottom of this page. If you are interested in supporting my campaign, please get in touch using the contact details below.

Since being re-elected I have continued to campaign on the local promises that I made: to bring local mental health beds back to Bedford; to fix Bedfordshire Police's unfair funding formula; and to fight for the local services residents need and use. With your support I will continue to do all I can to stand up for Bedford and Kempston.

I have grown up in North Belfast, a product of a mixed marriage, of a Catholic father from West Belfast and a Protestant mother from East Belfast.

I am proud to have been brought up in an inclusive family environment where difference and diversity are embraced and celebrated.

It is this ethos of equality which guides me when representing my clients as a practicing solicitor.

I am the youngest son of Patrick Finucane, who was killed 28 years ago.

Since his death, my family has campaigned for truth and justice, under the dignified direction of my mother Geraldine.

Now, by standing here in North Belfast, I am continuing the work my father started, towards a just, equitable and rights based society for all.

Paul Maskey has been a republican activist for his entire adult life.

He was first elected to Belfast City Council in 2001 when he topped the poll in the Upper Falls constituency.

Paul remained on the council until 2009 during which time he was Sinn Féin’s group leader from 2005 to 2007.

In 2007 Paul was first elected to the Assembly for West Belfast and then again in 2011.

In 2011 Paul was elected as MP for West Belfast in a by-election and was reelected again in 2015.

Paul is renowned for being a hard working MP who is easily accessible on the ground in West Belfast with his constituency office providing an excellent service to the people of the area.

Voters think too many politicians are all the same, straight from the Westminster bubble without real-world experience.

I don’t think it gets much more real-world than working as a Doctor in A&E or volunteering as a policeman and I have done both.

I have seen it all, believe me!

It taught me a lot about people and the problems they face.

And we don’t have enough people in Parliament who understand the challenges on the front lines of our public services.

My Mum was a nurse and my Dad was a policeman and growing up they taught me the importance of stepping up and serving.

I hope that gives you a good idea of my commitment to helping people & making a difference and I will always try and do that for you.

My Dad's family were farmers and we had a small holding when I grew up so I spent most of my weekends in the countryside. Its where I feel most at home.

Bexhill, Battle and the many villages that make up the constituency all have their own challenges and needs. It is my job to work all year round on those. Here are just some of the issues that residents talk to me about that are important to them:

CLEANING UP OUR WATER

The government has brought in new unlimited fines and the tightest ever  monitoring of discharges into our rivers and sea front. It is my job to relentlessly push the water companies to clean up their mess-no excuses.

SUPPORTING OUR FARMERS AND PROTECTING OUR COUNTRYSIDE

My Dad's family were farmers & growing up we were lucky enough to have a small holding so I spent most of my weekends in the countryside. Farmers put food on our tables & are stewards of our lands. I have campaigned for new laws to protect livestock from dog attacks & will oppose solar farms on prime farmland.

OPPOSING THE PLANS FOR THE NORTHEYE ASYLUM DETENTION CENTRE

I will always be willing to stand up for my constituents if the government gets things wrong. The plans for Northeye are not the right ones for Bexhill and I will do my best to get the Home Office to reconsider. You don't win on every issue but that doesn't mean you shouldn't try.

SECURING INVESTMENT IN OUR LOCAL HOSPITALS

I spent more than 10 years working on the frontline of the NHS as a doctor in A&E before entering politics. I wanted to use my experience to improve the NHS for all of us. Labour will freeze plans to invest in our local hospitals. I want to drive forward that investment so our staff are working in first class facilities.

BACKING OUR HIGH STREETS & BUSINESSES

I have spent time speaking to retailers about how I can better support our high streets in Bexhill, Battle and the villages. We need to back our police when they take a zero tolerance approach to shoplifting. We also need to make use of new laws to get absent landlords to work with us to fill vacant spaces.

FIGHTING ON LOCAL ISSUES THAT ARE IMPORTANT TO YOU

Each town and village will have local issues that are important to them. Whether it is speeding through our rural villages, houses being built in the wrong places, potholes on our roads or getting more public toilets opened in Bexhill - you tell me what is important to you and I will do my best to help.

But I want to hear your priorities. Complete my residents survey online and tell me what you think!

I look forward to speaking to as many of you as possible over the coming weeks of the campaign!

I have lived in Bexley all my life and in my twentieth year as a councillor in the London Borough of Bexley. My working career started in M&S’ Bexleyheath store and I spent eleven years working for the company working from Saturday staff to a store management position. I now run my own consultancy business and lives locally with my wife, a teacher, and our ten-year old twins.    I was Labour’s candidate in the 2021 Old Bexley & Sidcup by-election, achieving a 10% swing to the party. As the parent of a child with cerebral palsy, I work closely with local parent groups supporting and campaigning on behalf of children with disabilities and their families both across the borough and nationally with SCOPE and the Changing Places campaign.   During my time on the Council, I have served as Cabinet Member for Transport under the last Labour administration from 2003-06 where I worked with trade unions to save direct Bexleyheath to Victoria train services, deliver road safety improvements, and ensure the Elizabeth Line came south of the river to Abbey Wood. I have also served as Leader of the Labour Group on the council, as a local school governor and charity trustee.

I have lived in Oxfordshire for most of my adult life. I now live with my family in the Otmoor division, where I am heavily involved in the local community including as chairman of the governors at our local primary school. I am also a volunteer junior rugby coach. During the pandemic, I helped set up and administered a fund to support those negatively affected by COVID. My professional experience is in public policy making. For 13 years, I was a civil servant, working for the Treasury, Foreign Office, Department for International Development and Cabinet Office in London. Since 2012, I have held a senior leadership role at Oxford University, where I have helped to establish the Blavatnik School of Government. I am a keen cyclist, runner and walker, and am passionate about responding to the climate emergency and protecting our environment. Working in education and volunteering with young people, I want to ensure that every young person has the best start in life. As a community activist, I firmly believe that decisions are often best made at local levels and that, by listening respectfully and committing to find solutions, we can make things better together.
Preet Kaur Gill MP for Birmingham, Edgbaston is Shadow Minister for Primary Care and Public Health, and the UK's first female Sikh MP.

I was proud to be elected as the Member of Parliament for Birmingham Erdington in March 2022, when I became Birmingham's first ever black MP.

Erdington has been my home for over 35 years. It's where my children were born, raised, and attended local schools.

I'm a qualified nurse and worked at the local health centre at Warren Farm Road in Kingstanding for several years. I also served as a district nurse in Birmingham for 25 years.

At the next general election, we have a once-in-a-generation chance to secure real change for our community and our country. We must rebuild our NHS, public services and put more police officers onto our streets. We can only do this with a Labour Government.

statement_to_voters:
We have so much to be proud of in Birmingham: a super diverse community that tells the story of Britain's history, thriving small businesses providing jobs and driving our regional economy, and a hope that things can be better for our city and its people.



We've been let down by 14 years of successive Conservative governments - crime and antisocial behaviour is rising, our public services have been decimated, and divisive and damaging rhetoric at the top level of government is the new normal.



It doesn't have to be that way. We can put an end to Conservative rule, and put the voice of Brummies at the heart of the next government. But to do that, I need your support. This is the most important election in a generation: make your vote count.

Ayoub Khan is currently a Councillor for the Aston Ward which is part of the Perry Barr constituency. Ayoub declared that he would stand as an Independent following his reluctance to be silenced on the topic of Gaza by his former political party. Ayoub said that political leaders have a duty to represent the residents without fear. Politicians are slaves to the public and NOT political parties. In addition, Ayoub said that money wasted in foreign wars would have been better used in our Country where we have a crisis. The cost of living, crime, antisocial behaviour, homelessness, unemployment and health services are all key priorities for him if elected.

Ayoub is also a Barrister by profession and said that having a legal background will naturally allow him to advocate on behalf of all the residents.

favourite_biscuit: I like all the biscuits except Hobnobs which taste like sawdust.

statement_to_voters:
Bishop Auckland is my hometown, it's where we've put down roots and chosen to raise our family. I work in Research and Innovation at Durham University, my wife is a student midwife in the NHS, our kids go to local schools and colleges, and we're invested in the community.



I am standing to be our MP for the opportunity to serve and make a real difference for the people and place I love.



I admire people I meet every day who, despite being let down by a failing government, just get on with it: setting up businesses in a challenging economic climate, teaching in underfunded schools, treating patients in an understaffed NHS, and volunteering for neighbourhood clean-up teams, foodbanks, and youth clubs. But we are swimming against the current. After fourteen years of Tory government Britain is poorer, more unequal, and less influential in the world. We need a decade of national renewal to turn things around and MPs who serve the national interest, not their self-interest.



I've had a varied career in Business, Higher Education, and the Charity sectors. I studied Development Economics at Manchester University and have a strong interest in helping struggling economies to flourish -- including growing our local economy! I went on to specialise in conflict prevention and reconciliation, working in places affected by civil war, advising governments, charities, and the UN. So, my skills are in bringing people together to solve complex problems and build stronger communities.



I have also taught at school, college, and university levels, and I am passionate about helping our young people reach their potential, as I was helped in my teens by the policies of the last Labour government.



I don't come from money. My family struggled. I have been blessed with the opportunity of a great education but had to work 30-hour weeks on top of full-time study to pay my way through university. I have waited tables, stacked shelves, mopped floors, and laboured outside in all weathers. So, I know what it's like to support my family on low paid insecure work. Some of the people closest to me still do. I have fought my whole life, and I'll fight hard for everyone in our communities across Bishop Auckland, Crook, Shildon, and all the villages across Teesdale, and Weardale.

My name is Adnan Hussain, and this is my formal announcement of my intention to stand as an Independent Candidate for Blackburn in the upcoming Parliamentary election.

I am a Solicitor and a High Court Advocate practising in Blackburn.

-	I pledge to be a voice for all my community. 

-	I promise to make your concerns against the injustice being inflicted against the people of Gaza be heard in the places where our so-called representatives failed. 

I say no to supporting a genocide, instead its high time that we focus on our people here at home, whether that be the NHS, education or the current housing crisis. 

-	I promise to work towards bringing together all sections of my community here in Blackburn, to find common ground upon which we can all unite, and to listen to the voices of the marginalised, whether they be from the ethnic minority or white, working-class background.

-	I pledge to steer away from the politics of stigma within our town towards a place of inclusivity.

-	To help and encourage existing and new businesses throughout the town and to make Blackburn more inviting and open for them.

-	To work on making Blackburn the thriving hub it has the potential to be.

-	To work towards ending the housing crisis and bringing a future of stability for our younger generations.

-	To work on making Blackburn the thriving hub it has the potential to be.

I believe all my pledges combined have the potential to create more job opportunities and thus reduce poverty and crime.

I know that in my stance, I join a growing movement of individuals and smaller parties nationwide who will be stepping forward this July 4th to demand a different politics.

A politics of hope rather than misery and despair

A politics of inclusivity rather than the current culture wars being stoked by the mainstream parties to keep us divided and in fear and suspicion of the other.

Vote for me, Adnan Hussain, on July the 4th and let's come together to inject a sense of real community into our town.

I was born and bred in Fleetwood - where I still live today - and my track record as a campaigner and Labour activist is second to none. I have been proud to stand up and take on the Conservatives in Wyre and Lancashire and I am proud of what I have achieved, against the odds, in my community. 

I have represented my community for over 20 years on Wyre Council and I also serve on Lancashire County Council, where I am Deputy Leader of the Labour Group, and Fleetwood Town Council. 

As a working-class woman who has fought most of my life for my community - I believe I am the person we need to fight our corner. I have the passion, experience and dedication to fight for us all. I would be honoured to have your support to be our Labour candidate for Blackpool North & Fleetwood at the next general election.

Chris Webb is Blackpool born and bred, a true Sangrown'un. Chris lives in Blackpool South with his wife.

As the son of a Blackpool postman and teaching assistant, Chris has spent most of his adult life working in the public sector, following in their footsteps, most recently as the Deputy Police and Crime Commissioner for Lancashire.

As a leading voice in Blackpool's charity sector and a front-line public sector worker, he has a real track record of fighting for Blackpool's communities and continuing to put Labour values into action across Blackpool and has been awarded a Local Community Hero award for his charity work during the pandemic.

Chris has been fighting to eliminate child poverty in Blackpool for over a decade. He has been raising awareness, fundraising, and giving his time to help deliver 12,000 meals to local families each week through the food bank.

He's led the charge for improved mental health support for residents with the Blackpool Mental Health charity he helps lead as Chair of Trustees, which was awarded Blackpool Charity of the Year in June 2023.

When 800 local police officers were cut, as Deputy PCC, he launched new Police Task Forces to tackle local priorities, including drug dealing, anti-social behaviour, and burglary.

And when the Conservative MP for Blackpool South voted against free school meals, Chris stepped up and raised over £14,000 to ensure no child went hungry in the town that half term.

It’s been a huge privilege to serve as the Member of Parliament for Blaydon and to have delivered so much for my constituents, but I know we have so much more we need to achieve, that is why I will be campaigning to become the first Labour MP of Blaydon and Consett. The Conservatives have pushed our communities to the brink with successive years of funding cuts, they have neglected our region for too long. I will work to bring real investment into our area and my focus is on ensuring the communities of Blaydon and Consett can thrive. I want to hear from you and about your views. Our politics is always stronger when people engage with the process and I want to be your voice in Parliament for the Blaydon and Consett constituency.

I live on the West Sussex coast, with my husband, Chris.

I’m a well-connected, experienced political campaigner and fundraiser, and a successful senior business leader, specialising in technology and cybersecurity.

I’ve worked across multiple industries, volunteered as a trustee of a national charity, Meningitis Now, and I have observed US Primary elections as a guest of the US State Department.

I have a political background, but I’ve achieved this whilst building a successful business career, a broad voluntary portfolio, and a happy family life, with Chris, and my three step-daughters.

In short, I have gained an unusual breadth of experience and expertise. With such a varied life experience, I relate to and connect easily with people from every walk of life. I would love to use it to make our country, and Bognor Regis and Littlehampton, an even better place to live.

I’m standing to be our area’s first woman MP. I want to see our area thrive. I’ll be visible and accessible; once again our local voice in Westminster, never the other way around.  

A vote for Labour is a vote to turn the page on the chaos of the last 14 years. I’ll give our communities a seat at the table of the next Labour government, fighting for our area from the inside.

As your MP, I’d put my full support behind local campaigns on issues such as making sure our local miners finally get justice over their pensions, fighting for improvements at Junctions 28 and 29 on the M1, better local bus routes such as new route between Clowne and the Royal Chesterfield Hospital, and investment in our town centres.

Change will only come if you vote for it. Vote for change. Vote Labour on Thursday 4 July.

My roots and home are in Bolton. I'm raising my family here, and I want to make sure Bolton reaches its full potential.

With a strong track record of campaigning and knocking on doors for the Labour Party, and a history of working on life-changing campaigns for different communities - from our Armed Forces to victims of press abuse - I've got the experience necessary to be Bolton's voice in Westminster. Every time I speak to someone from Bolton they tell me the same story about their pride in our town, and how it's a great place to make a life, but sadly they tell me that the reality is the town has gone downhill in recent years. Bolton is being let down and left behind under the Tories.

I know that Bolton has so much potential and opportunity, and I'm determined to work with our communities, businesses, and local services to make sure Bolton delivers for everyone.

It's time for a change. Let me know if you want to play your part and join the team - I'd love to hear from you.

I'm Bolton born and bred. My Dad was a paramedic on Belmont Road, and my first job was working for the NHS at Bolton Hospital at a time when the last Labour government made record investment into our health service.

Yet after 14 wasted years, this government has eroded our public services, hollowed-out our town centres and widened inequalities.

It doesn't have to be like this. I have an ambitious, positive vision of a better Bolton West. One where power, wealth and opportunity are shared. Where everyone is able to realise their full potential, regardless of your background.

People across Bolton West deserve so much better. With a Labour MP and a Labour government, I know that together we can tackle the cost-of-living crisis, ensure investment in our towns, fix rising crime and the address the NHS backlog. That's why I want to carry on my family's tradition of public service in Bolton, as your MP.

If elected, I'll work with our local community groups, our councillors and with you to deliver on your priorities. And I'll ensure you have a powerful voice in Westminster.

If you'd like to find out more about me or can spare a few hours to help, please get in touch!

I'm not your typical politician. I come from a working class family and funded myself through college and university with retail jobs. I spend my professional career working outside politics in the voluntary sector as the chief executive of domestic abuse, mental health, and homelessness services. And I have a track record of delivering large climate infrastructure projects to achieve a green transition. I'm standing for Parliament to stand up for local people and help bring about a better Bournemouth and a better Britain.

Bournemouth is an amazing place, but the vibrant town I remember from my childhood has been let down by more than a decade of neglect by the Conservatives.

I have seen the decline of our high streets and town centre. I have felt the pain of rising energy bills and food costs. NHS waiting times are at record highs, and people like my grandparents have struggled to access quality local social care. Sewage is being pumped into our rivers and seas at an alarming rate. And crime is on the rise. The next election could not be more important. After 13 years of the Conservatives, it's time for change.

I don't come from a political family, but I was taught to value hard work, honesty and public service. Throughout my career, I've worked with businesses, governments and charities to solve problems and get things done. I've campaign on early years education, fair taxation and cost of living support. Now I want to deliver the best deal for people in Bournemouth West.

I believe that together we can win a Labour MP in Bournemouth West for the first time ever - and work to make sure Bournemouth fulfils its potential. I want to see a Bournemouth that builds on its reputation for innovation and creativity, that protects its environment and ensures it is the best possible place to live, work and visit.

Together we can build a brighter future for Bournemouth.

I am proud to be standing as Labour’s candidate in Bracknell, Crowthorne and Sandhurst, my home town. Only Labour can beat the Conservatives here, and only Labour will get Bracknell’s future back.   I’m not a career politician. Like my parents, I’ve worked my whole career in education. I’m a university lecturer and school governor, and I advise a national education charity on policy. Before that, I was a school teacher.   I’m standing to be Bracknell’s Labour MP because I want to re-build our public services and help families struggling with the cost of living crisis. After 14 years under the Conservatives, we need change.   I know first-hand what the Tories have done to our schools. We don’t have enough teachers, our kids’ mental health is suffering, and SEND students have been abandoned. On everything from the NHS to public transport, the environment to the cost of living, fourteen years of Tory government have robbed this country of its future.   In Bracknell, Crowthorne and Sandhurst, only Labour can beat the Tories. That’s why I am asking every voter to make a simple choice. More of the same with the Tories, or change with Labour.

Dawn, one of six children, was born and raised in East London to ex-pats from Jamaica. At a young age, she worked on a market stall as well as helping out at her family-owned bakery before starting her adult career as a computer programmer/systems analyst.

Dawn’s desire to enter politics came from a deep-rooted commitment to address inequality and strong values imparted by her parents. She soon went on to work as an equality and race officer at the GMB union and an adviser to the Mayor of London.

Elected as the Member of Parliament for Brent South on 5 May 2005 Dawn’s maiden speech described her constituency as a “shining example of integration at its best”. Dawn later became the first elected African-Caribbean woman to become a Government Minister in the UK.

Dawn has always been a passionate campaigner for young people; she is an Honorary Vice President of the British Youth Council, was chair of the All Party Parliamentary Group on Youth Affairs and was made a member of the Children, Schools and Families select committee and Vice Chair of the Labour Party with responsibility for Youth. In 2008 she became an Assistant Whip in the Commons before her work on youth led to Dawn being appointed as the Minister for Young Citizens & Youth Engagement at the Cabinet Office by Gordon Brown.

Based in the Cabinet Office the Minister’s role was to coordinate government work to help young people engage with politics which involved working with ministers in relevant Government departments including the Department for Children, Schools and Families (DCSF) and the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and other relevant bodies.

The recommendations of the Youth Citizenship Commission report were published in June 2009 and sought ways to help increase young people’s participation in their local communities as well as in local and national politics.

After a short break from elected politics, in which Dawn spent time working as a Magistrate and public speaker, Dawn ran a successful campaign in the 2015 General Election and won Brent Central back off the Liberal Democrats, securing a majority of nearly 20,000 – representing the largest vote swing in Britain at that election. She was again successful in the 2017 General Election, winning 73.1% of the vote.

A natural campaigner, since returning to Parliament Dawn has taken on the ‘Big 6’ energy companies over the excessive cost of pre-payment meters. She has held a Westminster Hall debate, launched a national petition and secured a commitment from the Prime Minister to look at this issue.

Dawn continues to commit her time in parliament to representing groups and people in society that are often underrepresented. In 2017 Dawn became the first MP in its history to sign a question in the House of Commons using British Sign Language. Dawn used sign language in her question to highlight the need to give the language full legal status. Dawn continues to run successful campaigns on Employment Tribunal Fees and is now pushing for the Government to publish full equality impact assessments on their policies.

Dawn was named the “most promising feminist under 35” by New Statesman magazine and was honoured as MP of the year at the 2009 Women in Public Life Awards. Since returning to Parliament Dawn was awarded two Patchwork Foundation awards, having been voted People’s Choice 2016 Labour MP of the Year and next receiving the Overall MP of the Year award in 2017. In 2020 named one of the 25 most influential women in the UK by Vogue.

Dawn served as Labour’s Shadow Minister for Women and Equalities between 2017-2020.

It has been my privilege to represent the people of Brent Central as your MP since being elected in 2015. As Parliament has now been dissolved after the General Election was called I am now no longer a Member of Parliament. I am now standing as the Labour candidate for Brent East.

My office has dealt with over 47,000 constituents’ queries and problems, and I’ve taken issues important to the people of this area right to the top – as with the Pre-Pay Rip-off campaign that has helped save money every day for families using pre-pay meters. I was also thrilled to be voted Labour MP of the Year by the Patchwork Foundation this year and DIVA magazine “Ally of the Year”. This was in recognition of my work to make Parliament accessible to all, because I truly believe that Parliament is there to represent the people of this country and should be working in the interests of the many, not the few.

I live near Ongar with my wife and our two children and for the past seven years I have been working as your local MP to help everyone in our local area. I will ALWAYS campaign on the issues that matter to you - whether that's supporting local business, fighting the pylons that threaten our countryside, pushing for tougher action against unauthorised development and fly tipping, or campaigning to retain local services at local hospitals.

In 2010 Brighton made history by electing Caroline Lucas as Britain’s first Green MP. Her impact has been phenomenal and support for her has only grown. People can see what a truly independent and strong representative can do, and I am working hard to earn each vote to prove that I can continue Caroline’s work.

From 2016 to 2024 I held the Labour Mayor to account in the London Assembly on the Transport, Housing, and Planning and Regeneration Committees. During this time, I was proud to strengthen the rights of renters, improve sustainable transport services, and help win much-needed new funding for youth services.

I was a councillor in Camden for 10 years and served two terms as co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales. These roles have combined to give me the experience to be an effective, independent MP.

I moved to London with an overdraft and a degree in 1997 and my previous, non-political work has been as a medical copywriter, PA, website manager, project manager for a digital start-up, author and transport campaigner.

Brighton deserves a powerful Green voice in Parliament, holding the next government to high account and championing the concerns of constituents. Since moving here last year, I’ve been delighted to make my home here and work hard for your vote to keep Brighton green.

Bristol is a city of unique opportunities. We have the potential to be a beacon to the rest of the country and the world, demonstrating how collective action can overcome even the most daunting challenges.

Our city is talented, hard-working, imaginative, and kind – values that I hope I will embody as your MP. I always aim to be a good listener with an open mind, and I strive to help wherever I can. As a former wind energy engineer, as the co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales, and a Bristol City Councillor between 2015 and 2024, I’ve dedicated my career to championing policies that will build a fairer, greener country.

The Conservatives can’t win here but I can. Unlike the current Labour MP, who has to agree with what Starmer says, my role as the Green Party leader allows me the freedom to advocate for what is truly right for our city. I won’t be swayed, coerced or intimidated into supporting a leader I don’t believe in. I would be free to listen to my constituents and vote with my conscience.

Casting a Green vote in Bristol Central is not just a vote against the Tories, it’s also a vote to hold Labour accountable to their promises, and a vote to champion progressive, green policies. A vote for hope.

Kerry has served as the MP for Bristol East since May 2005, winning re-election in 2010, 2015, 2017 and 2019. She currently serves on Labour's frontbench as shadow minister for Climate Change. The Bristol East Labour Party is regularly out campaigning and talking to local voters. This year will be crucial to ensuring that Bristol stays Labour in local elections and that we get the Labour Government this country is crying out for - and we'd welcome your support!

Karin Smyth was elected as Labour MP for Bristol South in May 2015, and currently is a member of the Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Select Committee. She has previously held the position of Shadow Northern Ireland minister and served on the Public Accounts Select Committee. She is also Chair of the Women's Parliamentary Labour Party and has provided maternity cover as Labour's Shadow Health and Social Care Minister.

Born in London to Irish parents who came to Britain in the 1950s, Karin moved to Bristol in the 1990s.

Before becoming an MP, Karin worked as a manager in the NHS. As MP for Bristol South, she has campaigned for better bus routes, improving access to local NHS services, working for access to abortion services for women in Northern Ireland, campaigned for assisted dying, safer communities and nation-wide safeguards on trailer safety.

Every year Karin co-hosts a Jobs and Apprenticeships Fair alongside key sectors in Bristol.

My name is Peter Fortune, and I am the Conservative London Assembly Member for Bexley and Bromley.

I grew up on a council estate in Lambeth and moved to Bromley in 2006, where I live with my wife, who works in education, and my two children.  I worked for many years for Newsquest media group across their London, Essex, and Sussex sites.

I was elected to Bromley council in 2010. I served as the executive assistant to the Environment before becoming Chairman of the Health and Wellbeing Board, and later joining the cabinet as portfolio holder for Children, Education and Families.

I was honoured to be the political lead for the turnaround of Children’s Services which received an Ofsted grade of ‘Good’ with ‘Outstanding Leadership’ in 2019.

I served as Deputy Leader of the Council from 2017 to 2021 and stood down as councillor for Hayes and Coney Hall in 2022 after being elected to the London Assembly.

On the London Assembly, I have served as Chairman of the Budget and Performance Committee and as Conservative Group Deputy Leader.

In my spare time I enjoy reading, walking, writing and cricket.  You may also sometimes find me shouting at a piano that refuses to play properly.

I live in Hoddesdon and attended primary school in Wormley. Growing up within our community has shaped my views and values and has made me the person I am today. 

I do not need need to move to Broxbourne to understand the issues that affect you as I'm already here, embedded in the community.

Until recently I was a local councillor and leader of Broxbourne Council and have a track record of standing up for residents.

I was first elected as a Councillor in 2018, and am currently a Councillor with the cabinet portfolio of Community Safety, Refugees and Equalities. I have had a long career working with or in the NHS. It was education that brought me into politics; specifically how we provide a fair and accessible education system and close the gap in education outcomes for neurodiverse people.

I'm proud to be Labour's candidate for the new Buckingham and Bletchley constituency at the next general election.



I grew up just over the border in Dunstable. My mum brought me up alone in a council flat, while she worked shifts in the Leighton Buzzard Morrisons.



Life wasn't always easy. Getting by on a low income, I watched my mum manage every paycheque to pay the rent and the bills, put food on the table, and give me as many opportunities as she could. Through her example, she passed on three simple values to me: hard work, aiming high, and never giving up.



Over the past year, I've seen first hand that those values are very much shared by local people, farmers, business owners, and civil society leaders across Buckingham, Bletchley, Tattenhoe, Winslow and the surrounding villages.



While people have hopes and aspirations for a better life for themselves, their families and their communities, they've told me they need a proactive MP who is on their side and can deliver change.



For over a decade, I've worked across the public, not-for-profit, and private sectors to shape economic policies that work for both ordinary working people and their families, and high-growth businesses in the industries of the future.



As your local MP, I'll use that experience to attract the investment, jobs and businesses which deliver higher incomes for local people, as well as fighting for the resources that gets the NHS back on its feet, ensures every child has the opportunity to thrive, and delivers clean energy.



We have a unique opportunity to reset the political conversation in our city, towns and villages. Please do get in touch. I'd love to hear your views about how we can build a better Buckingham and Bletchley together.

After 14 years of Conservative failure, decline and destruction of our public services, its time for change.

We deserve better. In Burnley, Padiham and Brierfield, our Conservative MP has not delivered the services, jobs, growth and ambition we need.



We need a fresh start.



Labour is proud of our towns and will make Britain a fairer, greener more prosperous place. We must invest in public services here; our high streets, our environment and our young people.



Together we can look to the future with confidence again. Take a fresh look at Labour.

I'm a local lad who is born and bred in Burton. Born at Queen's Hospital, I grew up in Stretton and went to local schools, William Shrewsbury and de Ferrers.   



My first job was collecting glasses at the Wetmore Whistle, and now I work in the fire and rescue service on campaigns to help keep people safe.  



I'm also a trade union rep within my workplace fighting for better pay and better jobs. I want to carry on fighting for working people as Burton and Uttoxeter's next Labour MP.



  I'm standing as our next Member of Parliament because the Conservatives have let us down and we can't afford another five years of their chaos.



We'll help local people by tackling the cost of living through reducing energy bills. Investing in local jobs and industries. Tackling crime by putting more police on our streets. Getting our NHS back on its feet and ending the lottery of getting a GP or NHS dental appointment. 



I believe we deserve better and it's time for change. We deserve a fresh start with Labour.

Like many of you, the NHS is in my bones. I am a surgeon and one of three generations of doctors who have served the NHS continuously since it began in 1948. My dad was an RAF medic in the war who joined the NHS when it started, and my son is an A&E doctor.

Our NHS has a brilliant and dedicated workforce of over one million people.  We need a government that listens to them. But after 14 years of a Conservative government our NHS is on its knees, and is in need of intensive care. Babies born today ought to live to a great age, with the amazing scientific discoveries happening every day, but in parts of our country life expectancy is falling; this should terrify us all. The solutions are political, not medical, and that’s why I want to be your MP. With your vote, I would become one of the few doctors in parliament.

Throughout Suffolk including Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket, our farms and factories produce food which feeds the nation, but under the Conservative government, farmers have lost out. The reality is there is no food without farmers, and we need a government that listens to our concerns about the future of farming and the workforce that work hard to produce our food.

After 14 years of the Conservatives, we are all worse off. Taxes are at a 70-year high, mortgages are up, and prices are up. We need economic stability to protect families, give businesses the confidence to invest again and make sure our high streets thrive.

The Labour Party has changed and we are ready to lead the change our country needs. Labour will stabilize the economy, cut NHS waiting times, increase the number of dentists and GPs, secure our borders, cut energy bills, put police on our streets, invest in schools, and protect our environment.

We need a serious leader and an end to the revolving door of unelected prime ministers. Sir Keir Starmer is a good honest man with a distinguished legal career. He is the leader this country needs – he is simply the best choice for Britain. The only serious choice.

With your support Labour really can win in Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket. Now is the time for serious decisions.

It is in the spirit of service that I write to you today, with the promise to put constituency and country first. Together we can turn the page, start to rebuild Britain and change our country. If you put your trust in Labour, we will deliver a brighter future. It would be the honour of my life to serve as your MP.

Please get in touch and consider joining the campaign. If you have not already done so, make sure to register to vote. In Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket, every vote will count.

party_name: Plaid Cymru - The Party of Wales

statement_to_voters:
As someone born and raised in the valleys, it is an honour to be elected to represent the community of Islwyn in Parliament. Brought up in the Rhondda valleys, I was educated at Porth County Comprehensive, Pontypridd College and Trinity College, Carmarthen where I graduated with a history degree.

Upon finishing university, I worked for Jack Brown (Bookmakers) Ltd before moving on to work for Lloyds TSB as a Personal Account Manager and then later working at the University of Glamorgan.

In 2004, I was appointed as a trade union official with the Union of Finance Staff where I campaigned to save finance and IT jobs from being off-shored.

Most recently, I spent four years working as parliamentary researcher to Don Touhig, the former MP for Islwyn, until his decision to stand down at the May 2010 General Election.

I have been a member of the Labour Party since the age of 15, holding positions at every level of the Party.  I am also a member of Unite, the Fabian Society and the Co-operative Party.

Having previously stood for Parliament in 2005 as the Labour candidate in Cheltenham, I was elected the Member of Parliament for Islwyn in 2010.

In my spare time, I enjoy reading, running as well as watching most sports.

Source: http://www.welshlabour.wales/chris_evans_mp

Jamie was elected as an MP in 2017.

Prior to his election, Jamie served as a Member of the Scottish Parliament (MSP) and a local councillor in the Highlands. In these roles, Jamie helped secure more money for home improvement grants and played a key role in preventing the downgrading of services at Caithness General Hospital. 

Outside of politics, Jamie has had a vast range of other jobs. From running his family’s cheese business and teaching English in Sicily to gutting fish in the Faroes and building oil rigs: his experience is diverse to say the least. 

Jamie enjoys spending time with his family, getting about the Highlands and playing Panto Dame at the local pantomime (yes, really).

Josh Fenton-Glynn was born and brought up in Calder Valley. He lives in Hebden Bridge with his wife and children and has been a councillor for eight years and is currently cabinet member for Adult Social care.



His work means he sees first hand the impact of this government's failure on local government. But also knows the potential of Calder Valley. Josh has said he wants to see a government that breaks down barriers to opportunities everywhere. That means supporting the thriving small business community in Calder Valley and making sure our children have schools we can be proud of.

I was born in Redruth and first went to Trewirgie School. My mum was an NHS nurse and my dad, Dr Charles Moon, was a GP in Camborne and Redruth for over 40 years.

Over the last year, I have listened to thousands of residents on doorsteps right across Camborne, Redruth & Hayle, and heard so many accounts of people struggling to make ends meet. Thirteen years of Conservative government failure have seen our public services cut to the bone, our economy collapse, a cost-of-living crisis with heating bills and food prices getting ever more expensive, and a meltdown in our NHS and social care system.

In my working life, I am a director of an electric vehicle charging point business that uses only sustainable energy. I liaise daily with local and national government to encourage them to roll our sustainable energy to reduce climate change.

Outside work, I am a keen environmentalist, a regular sea swimmer, a big Reds rugby fan, a youth coach and an amateur cricketer. I am passionate about ensuring that, once again, Camborne, Redruth & Hayle becomes a fantastic place to be raised, work, bring up a family and retire.

The Labour Party has a plan to restart our economy, create high skilled, sustainable jobs, build truly affordable housing, clean up our rivers and seas, deal with crime and anti-social behaviour and fix our NHS and social care services.

As a Redruth lad, Camborne, Redruth & Hayle is the only constituency I would ever represent. As your Labour candidate at the next General Election, nothing would make me prouder than having the opportunity to serve the communities that I know and love.

Local champion Daniel Zeichner is Cambridge's experienced MP.

As a life-long environmentalist Daniel is proud to be a shadow Environment Minister. It's a great job but what he really wants to be is the Environment Minister in Keir Starmer's next Labour Government with the power to make positive changes to tackle the climate emergency.

Daniel is a member of Greenpeace and has brought leaders on divestment to speak in Cambridge. He is also a bee fan -- he is a passionate Species Champion for the Ruderal Bumblebee and he campaigns to stop bee-killing pesticides.

After a decade of Tory rule, Cambridge people are suffering. There is a cost-of-living crisis and our public services have been cut to the bone. Daniel cares about social justice and he is a recognised Living Wage Foundation Parliamentary Champion. He has worked closely with students on the Cambridge University Living Wage campaign and with councillors to make Cambridge a proud Living Wage City.

As your MP, Daniel has been a leading voice for more funding for the police, against privatisation of local health services and for more cash for Cambridgeshire's NHS, including for better provision for mental health. He has led the campaign for fairer funding for Cambridge's schools and against cuts to nursery schools. He has been instrumental in securing laws to take back control of our local bus services.

As a constitutional reformer, Daniel backs an elected second chamber as well as votes at 16. Daniel is a patron of the Westminster Higher Education Forum, which aims to raise the quality of debate on public policy.

Daniel is Chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Data Analytics and he is a recognised Champion for the Internet Watch Foundation. He is also a national Champion for Cancer Research UK.

Daniel lives on Victoria Road in Cambridge with his partner Barbara, known as 'Budge', very close to where they lived when they met as students at King's College.

Before he became MP for Cambridge, Daniel had a variety of jobs in the public and private sectors, including working as a national officer for UNISON for 12 years to tackle women's low pay and racism. He also ran his own business.

Outside politics, Daniel enjoys football, live music and walking. He was, in his youth, a promising middle-distance runner. He is a Cambridge United season-ticket holder and he can often be found enjoying chamber concerts at Kettle's Yard.

Having lived and worked in Canterbury for over 20 years and raised my family here, it has been the greatest privilege to have been the Member of Parliament for the past two and a half years.

I am proud of what I have achieved -- fighting for our schools and the health service, campaigning on housing and climate change. But there is so much more to do, and I am putting my trust in the people of Canterbury, Whitstable and the Villages to re-elect me at the General Election and allow me to carry on the work that I have started.

I am standing on my record of standing up for Canterbury, Whitstable and the Villages. I hope that I can count on your support.

I'm proud to be seeking re-election as Cardiff Central's Labour Member of Parliament. Since being elected in 2015 I've worked hard to be an effective, accessible and independent minded voice for everyone in our area, helping tens of thousands of constituents. I live in Roath, in the heart of our vibrant, modern, multicultural capital city. Through my weekly advice surgeries and street surgeries, as well as working with Cardiff Labour Councillors and the Welsh Labour Senedd Member, residents know they have a committed Labour team in Cardiff Central, looking after their interests. In Parliament, I have held a number of roles on Labour's frontbench and I'm proud to serve as Shadow Secretary of State for Wales in Keir Starmer's Shadow Cabinet. I'm a lifelong trades unionist, Secretary of the Trades Union Group of MPs and a member of GMB, Usdaw and the Cooperative Party.

Stephen Doughty was elected as Welsh Labour & Co-operative Member of Parliament for Cardiff South and Penarth in a by-election in November 2012. He was re-elected in the General Elections of 2015, 2017 and 2019.

Born and educated in Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, he went on to study in Canada, Oxford and St Andrews, later working for the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly in Denmark, the National Assembly for Wales and then humanitarian NGOs World Vision UK, Oxfam, and as a special adviser on poverty, development, trade and humanitarian affairs to the then Secretary of State for International Development in the last Labour Government, Douglas Alexander.

Following the 2019 election, he was given the role of Shadow Foreign Affairs and International Development Minister, covering Africa initially, and is now Labour's Shadow Minister for Europe, North America and the Overseas Territories. He has previously held shadow ministerial and other roles in the Shadow Treasury, Business and Foreign Affairs teams, was also an Opposition Whip, and has served on the Wales, International Development and Home Affairs Select Committees.

He has been active in the HIV/AIDS, Global LGBT+ Rights, Steel, Armed Forces and a number of other APPGS. He also co-chairs the Parliamentary Labour Party LGBT+ Group. He has completed the Armed Forces Parliamentary Scheme and studied at the Royal College of Defence Studies.

A LOCAL, EXPERIENCED, CONFIDENT VOICE FOR CARLISLE

My family have lived in Carlisle for generations. Walk across Eden, Harraby or St Nicholas bridges and you'll find my Great Grandfather's name on the plaque commemorating their opening. My mam was a Carr's cracker packer and later a homehelp. After serving in the second world war, dad worked as a painter and decorator at Norweb.

I grew up in a small terraced house in Denton Holme, went to Robert Ferguson and Trinity schools and my first fulltime job was at 14MU. Like other working class families, mine believed in working hard to give your children a better future. I was the first person in my family to go to university. After graduating, I - like many of our young people - moved away from Carlisle for work. I managed an MP's office, responding to hundreds of constituent enquiries. That's why I know that being an MP isn't a part-time job. It's the job. And it's time Carlisle had a fulltime MP.

I worked in the voluntary sector, campaigning for disabled people and for laws to safeguard children. As a senior manager in industry I shaped policies and regulation to protect millions of consumers.

I'm the mother of a student nurse so I don't need to watch the news to know that the Tories have pushed our doctors, nurses, paramedics, health assistants and care staff to breaking point. After 14 years of Conservative failure waiting lists are never ending, seeing a GP is increasingly difficult and local people have more chance of winning the lottery than they have of registering with an NHS dentist. Yet again the Conservatives have proved that our health service is not safe in their hands.

In 2021 I founded a charity to save Carlisle's Victorian Baths because I have confidence in our city. I have confidence that a Labour Government will unleash the potential of our city. And I am confident that I have the experience to be a strong voice for our city in Parliament.

Get in touch and let's realise Carlisle's potential together.

Bobby lives just off Green Wrythe Lane in Carshalton with his wife Gemma and dog Chester.

He was raised on a council estate, the son of a cleaner and a scaffolder, and now runs his own small business advising charities tackling global poverty.

It’s his family’s work ethic that inspires Bobby to roll up his sleeves and get things done for the community. He is passionate about making a difference, serving as a local Councillor and leading the fight to protect St Helier Hospital.

Bobby is hoping to follow in Tom Brake’s footsteps, working hard right across the constituency and always being on hand to help.

I am Patrick Spencer, the Conservative Party’s Prospective Parliamentary Candidate for Central Suffolk and North Ipswich. I live in Suffolk with my wife Anna and two sons. My happiest childhood memories were spent on the Aldeburgh seafront, playing at Ufford Park, or watching Ipswich play at Portman Road.

Suffolk is indeed a wonderful place to live, and as the MP for Central Suffolk and North Ipswich I want to work to keep it that way. That means working with Government to deliver more funding for our local NHS services, supporting both our Police and Crime Commissioner and Suffolk Constabulary to tackle crime and anti-social behaviour, and arguing for a fairer funding deal for schools in Suffolk so that our young people get the best start in life possible. I want to make sure residents are supported and protected from the effects of severe flooding, and make sure their voice is heard when they object to unnecessary developments that blight our beautiful countryside. And I want to champion businesses across the constituency, large and small, so that we continue to create jobs and economic opportunity here in Suffolk.

Outside of politics I am a Senior Fellow at the Centre for Social Justice, a Trustee of the Jobs Foundation and a Governor at my local Primary School. Sarah works to protect our natural environment and for action on climate change. In 2023 she tabled a Private Members Bill for the Protection of Chalk Streams. Sadly it fell at the Second Reading when time ran out for the Parliamentary session. She re-presented it to Parliament in early 2024 and though this also ran out of time for debate before the 2024 General Election was called, Sarah continues to work across Party lines with MPs from different parties to try to implement protections for these precious, rare ecosystems.

A key election pledge that Sarah made when she was elected was to hold HS2 to account. She has been true to her word and has raised many individual complaints with HS2 on behalf of residents, including environmental concerns, noise and traffic problems arising from the works and many more. She has spoken several times in Parliament about concerns over HS2 including calling for the project to be scrapped as the business case continued to collapse with the announcement of further project delays and the cancellation of the northern phase. She played a key role, working with Missenden Parish Council and Amersham Town Council, in uncovering the misuse of a water hydrant by HS2 contractors in Summer 2022.

She has built a reputation as a vocal campaigner for justice for victims of the surgical mesh scandal. After meeting with a constituent who had undergone surgical mesh implantation and suffered horrific consequences, Sarah has raised the issue several times in Parliament. She is Vice Chair of the All Party Parliamentary Group on the Mesh scandal. The victims are mostly women and many have been left in appalling pain.

In 2023, working with an MP from the Scottish National Party, Sarah co-founded a new All Party Parliamentary Group on Crohn's disease and Colitis.
