statement_to_voters: Emma Hardy grew up in the East Riding of Yorkshire a few miles from the seat she now represents. She has lived in her constituency seat of Kingston-upon-Hull West and Hessle for nearly 20 years. Before becoming an MP, Emma was a local primary school teacher for over ten years. She was first elected in 2017 and now sits on the influential Treasury Select Committee and chairs a number of All-Party Parliamentary Groups which reflect her interests in education, social inclusion and women's health. Emma continues to pursue legislative improvements to property flood protection and insurance, driven by the city's devastation in the 2007 floods and the threats of climate change. Her belief in positive local action has seen her establish projects to tackle the cost of school uniform and to increase urban biodiversity. In 2022 she launched "Work Hull, Work Happy," which aims to establish Hull as the remote working capital of the UK.

party_name: Alliance - Alliance Party of Northern Ireland

statement_to_voters: Cat has been the Labour MP for Lancaster and Fleetwood since 2015 and is lucky enough to live in this beautiful part of Lancashire with her young son. Cat has been an active local MP campaigning for and securing funding for flood defences after Storm Desmond, speaking out against fracking in Lancashire, and championing schools including small and rural schools. She meets regularly with local businesses and individuals frequently taking up issues on their behalf with Government ministers as well as holding regular 'Chats with Cat' in villages and street surgeries in the urban parts of this diverse constituency.

I have lived most of my life in Leeds. I was born here, on the University Campus. My family moved south when I was young, when Thatcher’s cuts forced them to chase jobs wherever they could. But I chose to return to Leeds as a student, and moved to Headingley. I studied Information Systems at the University of Leeds and was elected as the Full Time Finance Officer of Leeds University Union in my final year.

I joined the Labour Party in 1997, and have been an activist ever since. I joined the party because of its ideals of equality and social justice, and I remain committed to those ideals. I have been active at every level of the party and am currently a Councillor for Meanwood and Moortown areas of Leeds.

I have worked as a Community Development Worker in Hyde Park, Headingley and Weetwood, and other areas of the City. I was a member of a succesful team which put together the bid for Leeds’ largest Surestart Scheme - for Little London, Woodhouse and Meanwood. This was a crucial step in helping to establish the Surestart programme here in Leeds. I have also helped to establish and develop many new community organisations all over the City.

I now work with social enterprises, supporting groups and individuals to set up social enterprises and running the regional body Social Enterprise Yorkshire and the Humber representing social enterprises and co-operatives. I am very proud of the part I’ve been able to play in establishing more than 200 co-operatives and social enterprises across Yorkshire, and in helping them to grow and develop.

I was elected to Leeds City Council for Moortown and Meanwood in May 2012. In that role I have been active in many local campaigns and achieved improvements in the environment and services for local people bringing in traffic calming schemes and helping secure the first new park in North Leeds for over 50 years.

I am deeply committed to Leeds and its people, and to the Labour Party and its ideals. I am standing for election in Leeds North West because I believe those ideals have the answers to the problems people here face, and because I want to put my experience and commitment to work for local residents.

Richard is the Labour Party Candidate for East Leeds. He was first elected as the Member of Parliament for East Leeds in 2015.

He lives in East Leeds and his family has lived and worked in East Leeds for more than 100 years -- ever since arriving from Ireland looking for work.

He takes duty of being your Member of Parliament very seriously. That's why he promised not to take any second jobs and to hold regular and accessible advice sessions for local residents right across East Leeds. He has kept those promises.

Richard has helped thousands of local people in East Leeds facing tough times through no fault of their own.

Every vote for Richard is a vote for a strong local voice - from East LEEDS, for East Leeds. It's a vote to ensure East Leeds is not forgotten.

It has been an honour to serve the people of North East Leeds in Parliament since 1997. I have always championed our rich diversity and campaigned for a better life for all residents based on fairness, justice and equality. It would be a privilege to be re-elected so I can continue my work to improve the lives of everyone in North East Leeds. Homeowners, renters, the homeless and everybody in between needs a Labour government which is driven to deliver for people across North East Leeds and I look forward to playing my part in that.

I'm the Labour Party candidate for Leeds North West, a new parliamentary constituency, where I was born and raised.

I've spent my life campaigning for change.

Whilst working at Friends of the Earth, I co-led the campaign for what became the world leading Climate Change Act, a legally binding framework to reduce emissions across our economy. The campaign united people who had never worked together before and became the fourth most supported motion in parliamentary history. I went onto lead our international climate change engagement work at the Department of Energy and Climate Change, supporting Ed Miliband at the UNFCCC conference. I became executive director at WWF-UK where I pioneered work on low carbon transition plans for the biggest companies in the UK. 10 years ago I was awarded an OBE for services to tackling climate change in the UK and overseas. There is much more to do - to address the threat and garner the opportunity - and I want Leeds to be at the forefront of the Green Industrial Revolution.

I want to help

1. Get Britain building again, so we can have the clean energy supplies of the future, bringing our costs down and ensuring sources of UK energy.

2. Switch on Great British Energy, so the country - and our public services - are benefitting from our investment in a national energy supply.

3. Getting the NHS back on its feet - I have a strong interest in mental health; I want to focus on improving support for mental health of young people within our constituency.

4. Take back our streets - so our high streets, small businesses and communities are thriving.

5. Break down barriers to opportunity - so every primary school family can access a breakfast club; we introduce a broader curriculum so our children become fitter for the future and expand training in skills and apprenticeships.

Mark is Labour's candidate for Leeds South West and Morley. He grew up in a terraced house on Churwell Hill, went to Morley High School and now raises his family in the new part of the constituency, Farnley and Wortley. He's a teacher at a local South Leeds school and a councillor, working to improve the lives of people accross Farnley and Wortley.

As a teacher, Mark see's first-hand how our young people are being held back by the Tories. Leeds South West and Morley deserves an MP who will fight to ensure that every child in every classroom in every school can fulfil their true potential.

Mark's Priorities:

\- Urgent action on the cost-of-living crisis

\- Giving every young person the best start in life

\- More police on the streets to keep us safe

\- Building a NHS that is there when we need it

\- Public transport that works for everyone

\- Support for our local businesses and town centers

\- Protecting our parks, rivers and green spaces

I love our country and I love our community. 

I’m proud to live in Pudsey, and with me as your Labour MP in Leeds West and Pudsey and a Labour Government across our country, I know we can be so much better.   As the MP for Leeds West since 2010, I’ve proven that I have a strong track record of being a local champion, leading campaigns to save Bramley Baths, open a new station at Kirkstall Forge and so much more. As Shadow Chancellor, I have also got a powerful national voice to stand up for working people.   If you elect me on Thursday 4 July, I promise to be a local champion and a national voice for you.

Hello, I am Shockat Adam, and I am honoured to be your independent candidate for Leicester South. My roots run deep in this city, having been raised, educated, and now working here. Leicester South isn’t just a place where I conduct business; it’s my heart , home, and commitment. 

For over 15 years, I have been privileged to serve our community through my award-winning optical practice and my community work.  This has given me a unique perspective on our city’s challenges and opportunities. I have witnessed firsthand the struggles of hard-working individuals and families as they try to make ends meet in the face of a rising cost of living. I have seen the strain on our NHS as it copes with increasing demand and limited resources. I have watched local businesses, our economy’s backbone, struggle to survive in an increasingly competitive market. I have seen the impact of neglect on our environment as we fail to take the necessary steps to protect and preserve it for future generations. But I also believe that Leicester South is a city of immense potential. We are a diverse and vibrant community, rich in culture and history. We have a strong sense of community spirit and a willingness to work together to overcome challenges. I believe that by harnessing these strengths and working together, we can build a brighter future for our city.

As your representative, I am committed to putting the needs of Leicester South first. I will not be beholden to party politics or special interests. My loyalty lies with you, the people of Leicester South. I will listen to your concerns, advocate for your needs, and work tirelessly to ensure that our city is a place where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. I am passionate about creating a fairer, more inclusive, and prosperous Leicester South. I believe that by working together, we can make this vision a reality. I am excited to embark on this journey with you, and I am confident that together, we can build a brighter future for Leicester South.

Please do not hesitate to contact me to share your concerns, ideas, or suggestions. I am here to listen, and I am here to serve you. Thank you for being so supportive, and I look forward to working with you to make Leicester South an even better place to live, work, and raise a family.

Shockat Adam

statement_to_voters:
I love our city and it has been the honour of my life to serve as the MP for Leicester West. From backing our schools and hospitals to campaigning for decent jobs, homes and more police, I've always put local people first.



Every week people tell me about the struggles they face to pay the bills, get to work or even see their GP. It doesn't have to be this way. Labour has a plan to get our city and country growing again. We'll work with businesses to create good jobs that pay a decent wage, invest in our local NHS and schools, and recruit more police to make communities safe.



We need a Labour government to make the changes our city desperately needs and that is why I am again standing as the Labour candidate for Leicester West.

Our country is in desperate need of change. The NHS is in crisis, families are struggling with the cost of living and sewage is being dumped in our rivers and seas. I'm campaigning to deliver change for our communities and our country.

I am a long-term resident of Lewes constituency. I’ve lived here for 20 years, initially in Lewes where I was a councillor for Malling and the town centre, and more recently I call the town of Newhaven home. I am a councillor at Town, District and County levels in Newhaven and live here with my partner and two young children. I am deeply committed to our community; to ensuring there is prosperity for all, a decent education for our children, and our green spaces, rivers and seas are protected. Let me share my track record:

1. I've been a Councillor in Lewes constituency since 2007: Over the years, I’ve immersed myself in our community, understanding its challenges and aspirations first-hand.

2. I've been Leader of Lewes District Council (2020 and 2022): tackling the cost of living crisis, ensuring significant funding for play area improvements, gaining funding for the regeneration of Newhaven, supporting local businesses, and supporting biodiversity and our green spaces leading to tangible improvements in people’s lives.

3. I was a champion of the People’s Vote: As Campaign Director of the European Movement, I spearheaded the People’s Vote campaign alongside other pro-European organisations.

4. I'm an education advocate: I fight passionately for fully funded pupil premiums and against the Government’s two-child benefits cap.

Lewes Constituency is a beautiful and vibrant place – from our coastal towns of Seaford and Newhaven, Polegate and Willingdon, our historic coastline and county Town of Lewes and our wonderful villages. And these are hugely exciting times for our constituency. 

We are one of the top ten target seats in the country for the Liberal Democrats. The Conservatives have a very slim majority of less than 2,500 votes over the Liberal Democrats here. Polls are showing the Liberal Democrats can win here. That means every vote matters. With your help, I can win. And, together, we can continue building a better future for our community.

I've lived in Lewisham for over 20 years with my husband and two children, who attend local schools.

My parents came to Lewisham as part of the Windrush generation. We lived in a council home which we valued hugely. After 8 years as a local councillor, I've been proud to represent our community in Parliament since June 2018. I will continue to be your local champion, tackling the issues that matter to you.

It has been a huge privilege to serve as MP for Lewisham Deptford (which becomes Lewisham North at the general election) since 2015. I have lived in the constituency for over 20 years, and it is a joy to represent the people and places I have got to know in that time.



"For me, politics has always been local. Prior to being elected to Parliament, I served as a local councillor in Brockley ward and was chair of the Lewisham Council Labour group. I also worked for a trade union for 13 years and during my time there led campaigns against low pay, the exploitation of agency workers and the use of zero-hour contracts.



"My priority is to give my constituents a voice in Westminster, whether that's by fighting for decent housing, defending our NHS, lobbying for school funding, or protecting our environment. I have also campaigned for youth violence to be treated as a public health issue and in doing so set up the cross-party Youth Violence Commission.



"I have held several front bench roles, including almost four years spent as a whip and a stint as Shadow Minister for Civil Society. In April 2020 I was appointed Shadow Minister for Disabled People and I remain in that role today. I am incredibly proud of what I have achieved so far and look forward to hopefully continuing that work in government

Ellie Reeves is MP for Lewisham West and Penge, having been first elected in 2017. Before entering Parliament she was an employment rights lawyer for over a decade. She also served on Labour's National Executive Committee for 10 years and was vice-chair of the London Labour Party. In 2020 she was appointed Shadow Solicitor General, in December 2021 was promoted to Shadow Justice Minister, and is now Deputy National Campaign Coordinator.

Born in Zambia and raised in London, I come into politics having served 24 years in the RAF. During my service I advocated for greater diversity in the armed forces, delivered humanitarian relief in Haiti and the Philippines, and led the 2021 air evacuation of Afghanistan. I am passionate about education and opportunities for our young people in Leyton & Wanstead. If elected, my top priorities will be the delivery of a new Whipps Cross hospital, addressing the open drug use problem and ensuring the next generation have the same opportunities I was given.

It is an honour to again be selected as the Labour party candidate for Lichfield constituency. Lichfield has been my home since before I learned to call a place home. I have had the absolute privilege over the last 33 years to learn in our local schools, shop on our local high streets and call many of our neighbours lifelong friends.

We are blessed to live in such a beautiful and historic part of our country, with stunning natural environments in places like Chasewater, Admaston, and along the Trent; with amazing architecture in the historic centre of Lichfield and in many of our villages; with the amazing people and communities that call Lichfield, Burntwood and our villages home, and who truly make our constituency all that it is.

Over the last 14 years, though, we have all seen our local area be let down by successive Conservative governments. The closure of local doctors’ surgeries, police stations and community venues; the lack of investment in our schools and our economy; the absence of any action on sewage spills in our waterways; a total failure to respect and support our high streets; and the worst cost of living crisis in living memory.

But it doesn’t have to be this way, we can rebuild and renew the infrastructure we rely on and the bonds between our community. That’s why I’m proud to be standing on a Labour Party platform offering a decade of national renewal, and for a mission led government that will change Britain for the better.

Together, on 4th July, we can turn a page on the inaction, sleaze and crisis of the last decade and half, we can vote for change which will get the NHS back on its feet, support our high streets and properly value our natural environment. On 4th July we will all have the power to vote for change and for a brighter, more hopeful future.

It is an honour to be standing for re-election as your Labour Candidate for Liverpool Wavertree.

It is time for change. Only I and a Labour Government can deliver that change for Liverpool Wavertree.

This is the place where I was born. This is the place I have worked hard for to make your voice heard in Westminster.

My plan – Labour’s plan – is to end the years of Tory decline and hardship to instead return us to years of opportunity and growth.

Together we will improve our schools. Put an end to families being left without a home. Stop cuts to vital services like social care and long waits for healthcare. Bring an end to the cost of living crisis.

I hope I am given the chance to continue delivering for you, for our community.

People right across Livingston constituency are hopeful for the future. Of course we are, it's a wonderful place to live and bring up a family. But we need an MP and government that's on our side.



After well over a decade of the SNP and Tory governments, people across Livingston constituency are asking: have our lives got better?



It's time for a fresh start.



We need a government that is focussed on what matters to you and your family: properly funding our NHS and schools, building an economy that works for working people, getting police back on our streets, and helping families with the cost-of-living crisis. I will stand up for you - and be an MP who works tirelessly to make sure everyone, no matter their background, can thrive.



Vote Labour for the change Scotland needs.

Despite today's difficulties, I am hopeful and determined. Hopeful about the prosperous, greener future we can build. Determined to help deliver it.



I've devoted my life to making families better off. That's why I became an Economist, taught in schools, and was a trade union rep.



I became an Economist so I could make families more prosperous. I learnt my trade in the Treasury and gained a PhD. In my current day job at a think tank, I work on policies that will ensure every person in this country has enough money to thrive, public services they can rely on, and a Green New Deal that will get us to Net Zero with good jobs across the country.



I also spent two years working to end poverty inside the Somaliland government, one of the poorest and most fragile nations on earth. A nation where climate change is already leading to devastating droughts and starvation. I co-wrote their National Development Plan, economic policy, and budgets to help put them on the path to prosperity.



I've also taught children in disadvantaged schools. That doubled the chances of those kids getting into good universities. And as a trade union rep, I organised my members and stopped a 33% pay cut for my low-paid colleagues.



Service and hard work can create a better future. Those are the British values my family taught me. My grandfather served in the war, my parents started a business. Those are the values that I've lived my life by.



Those values are why I'm working so hard to win this election. To serve the people of Loughborough, Shepshed, and the Villages. To work tirelessly for a better, greener future.



Let's build that better, greener future together.

I work in the voluntary sector, and was previously Political Advisor to Dame Tessa Jowell. I grew up partly in Cavenham, in Suffolk, before moving to Gorleston in Great Yarmouth, just along the coast.

I worked in a coalition of campaigners to amend the Domestic Abuse Bill which resulted in children being listed in their own right as victims of domestic abuse, and helped to convince the Government to introduce England's first ever domestic abuse code word, Ask for ANI, for victims who need to flee dangerous perpetrators.

I'm passionate about fighting for the causes I believe in. As the MP for Lowestoft, I would be a fierce advocate for change at a local and national level. We must fix our crumbling infrastructure, put Lowestoft at the heart of Labour's green industrial revolution, and tackle the cost of living crisis.

Half of all residents in our constituency are cutting back on food and energy, and Lowestoft in particular has high rates of deprivation and wards where one in four children live in poverty.

People in Lowestoft need a local champion who will fight for change in Parliament. As our Labour candidate and MP, I promise to put the needs of our community first.

Luton is my home and I love it. From railways to healthcare to policing, the country needs a lot of fixing. A Labour government will oversee a decade of national renewal to get the UK back on track. 

In five years as Luton North's MP, I successfully campaigned for lifts at Leagrave station, supported hundreds of local small businesses, proposed laws on miscarriage bereavement leave and fireworks regulation, voted for tougher knife crime laws and a ceasefire in Gaza. I have answered over 20,000 individual calls for help. If re-elected I will continue to put Luton North first.

Luton North deserves a government that will work for us, bringing bills down, tackling antisocial behaviour and fixing the NHS. A vote for Labour will help achieve this.

As the MP for Luton South since 2019, it is a privilege to stand again as the Labour candidate for the new constituency of Luton South & South Bedfordshire.

Bedfordshire is my county, and Luton is my home. I was born in the Luton & Dunstable hospital and have lived in Luton almost all my life. Before entering Parliament, my career as a senior public sector manager gave me valuable insight into the world of work and being a local councillor for nine years gave me a deep understanding of public service.

I’m proud of our area and all our communities, be they urban or rural. Yet everyone I speak to feels that nothing works anymore.

After 14 years of economic chaos under the Conservatives, working people are worse off. Living standards are down. Crime goes unpunished. Ambulances don’t come. Schools crumble over our children’s heads. Sewage floods our waters. Mortgages and food prices are through the roof.

There’s a clear choice at this election: more chaos with the Tories, or stability with Labour. We need to turn the page and start to rebuild our country. Labour has a long term, serious plan to change Britain.

I'm proud to be from Macclesfield. My mum and her mum before her, worked in our local NHS and I went to school in Poynton. It's a great area with great people, but Macclesfield has been taken for granted by the Conservatives for too long.



Our communities are confronting immense challenges: from the cost of living crisis to decaying public services, and the issue of our time -- the climate emergency. All of us have seen the decline of our town centre and the lack of attention paid to our rural communities. Meanwhile, prices are up and living standards are down. We face record NHS waiting times in Cheshire East and schools literally crumbling while the government stands by. As we've seen with the Bollin, sewage is being pumped into our rivers at an alarming rate. And our country's reputation abroad is at rock bottom.



The next election is an opportunity we don't want to miss. After 14 years in power, the Conservatives have crashed our economy, decimated our public services, and lost people's trust. Together we have a chance to have a Labour representative in parliament for the first time ever -- an MP who works for all our communities. I've beaten the Tories in their own backyard, now I want to do the same for my hometown. I want to see an area that's no longer neglected but supported to be the best possible place to live, work and grow old.

Together we can build a brighter future for Macclesfield.

Joshua Reynolds is a familiar face across Maidenhead. Elected to the council in 2019, and now a cabinet member, Josh grew up in Courthouse Road and went to Alwyn, Courthouse and Furze Platt Senior Schools, only leaving to study in Cardiff where he graduated with a first-class degree in Business and Management Studies. On his return, he successfully managed a chain of supermarkets before taking the decision to devote himself full time to public service.

Joshua’s time in retail gave him a valuable insight into the cost-of-living crisis. He saw first hand how the crisis impacted his shoppers, and how the increase in shoplifting has hit local businesses. 

He is also campaigning to see the walk-in centre re-opened at St Mark’s Hospital and the improvement and expansion of health services there and around the constituency to support the fast-growing population. 

Joshua sees river pollution as another key issue and is calling for the water companies to be held to account for polluting our waterways. He fully supports the Lib Dem pledge to transform water companies into public benefit companies, ban bonuses for water bosses until the pollution ends, and replace Ofwat with a tough new regulator with much greater powers.

As a long-time resident of Mansfield, I have witnessed first-hand how lives change for the better when we have a Labour MP and Government.

As a parent with children in Mansfield during the 1997-2010 Labour Government, I saw the profound impact that action by Labour in government can have on working-class families. It gave my family access to high quality education, the lowest NHS waiting times ever and a growing economy that made our lives better.

I want to inspire the people of Mansfield with a fresh message that Labour is on their side, upholds their values, and wants them to win. I have the drive and resilience to win here and the values and experience to match.

Like many areas across our country, Mansfield isn't thriving right now, but it can with a Labour MP under a new Labour Government.

As a volunteer, active member of our community and lifelong trade unionist, I have always strived to make things better. From being a school governor, volunteering for local charities that make a difference for adult social care and domestic violence, and supporting our local Credit Union. I've organised, campaigned and delivered positive change throughout my life.

Our shared values are under threat right now. We have a Tory MP who doesn't live here and doesn't act in our interests. For 14 years we have had Conservative Government that has failed us.

I am now asking for your vote, and your faith in me, to become the Labour Member of Parliament for Mansfield. Together, we can make a real difference for our community.

I live just outside St Davids, but I grew up in a farming family and have spent many Easters lambing and many summers doing the harvest. Professionally, I trained and practised as a barrister, specialising in healthcare, public and employment law, before leaving to work as an organiser for a grassroots trade union that helps cleaners campaign for better pay and working conditions. My values are hard work, community and caring for others. I am committed to Pembrokeshire and want to be an MP that is embedded within our local community, using my skills to fight for a kind, caring and compassionate society where everyone is valued.

I'm Greg Smith, your local Conservative candidate for the new Mid Buckinghamshire constituency, covering the market towns of Princes Risborough, Wendover, and the surrounding villages. I live here in Chearsley, with my young family, and want to make our beautiful part of the country an even better place to live, work, and bring up a family. I'm here to help, so please don't hesitate to get in-touch.

I have lived in Mid Cheshire for most of my adult life. It's where my children were born, and it's where I've been proud to represent as a Councillor for the last ten years during some of its most challenging times.

In Mid Cheshire, we have one in five children living in poverty. A child born in my ward in Leftwich will have a life expectancy ten years lower than one born just a couple of miles away on the other side of town.

I've chosen to dedicate my life to our community because I believe that every child should have the opportunity to reach their full potential.

To fight the pernicious idea that your background, your circumstances, who you know, where you come from might shape your life more than your talent, your creativity, or your determination.

This aspiration for the next generation is what's at stake at the next election. Get involved in my campaign, and let's win a better future - together.

We need a fresh start in Middlesbrough South & East Cleveland. I'm proud to have grown up here, and serve the community as a councillor and cabinet member. I started out as a teacher here, before working in education and economic policy nationally. I've seen first-hand how our people are hurting after thirteen years of Conservative government - and a Conservative MP who helped Liz Truss crash the economy. That's why I'm standing to be our next MP: to get a fresh start and a better deal for our home. It's time for change!

I moved to Dorset in 1999 when I accepted a promotion when I worked in financial services. We have since raised our four children here – three of whom are now adults. It was my experience as a local business owner that got me interested in politics – as chair of the chamber of commerce I engaged regularly with councils, and this helped develop my voice representing others.  After being elected to Poole Council I helping write several policies including the Anti-Bullying Strategy and the Seafront Strategy. When BCP Council was formed I became leader, working across seven political groups, and took the council through the dark days of Covid-19. More recently as leader I have averted a financial crisis to deliver a balanced budget and developed the new Local Plan. This will ensure the housing we need for the next generation is delivered with the infrastructure it needs, minimises the environmental impact and protects the green belt our community treasures. When Annette Brooke announced her retirement from Parliament I was selected to run for MP and I have been campaigning for a better deal for Dorset ever since, using the skills gained in the councils and through my community work including as a school governor, chair of neighbourhood watch and youth club lead. Government is failing to support local communities or provide fair funding so the right public services can be delivered. From crumbling school buildings to broken promises on expanding our community hospitals, councils having to bid for enough money to repair our roads and a lack of police officers in our neighbourhoods, things just do not work anymore. I will use my voice as a Liberal Democrat MP to fight to resolve Dorset’s dental desert – starting with children and the vulnerable. There are enough dentists here, but their contract means many are leaving the NHS. People do not want to work in the care sector because they can earn more working in supermarkets so we will increase their minimum wage. We will also provide free personal care, so no one must struggle with simple tasks of washing and eating. Liberal Democrats believe that delivering this – something that is already done in Scotland – will reduce the need for hospital admissions and improve the lives of older people. We are lucky to live in such a beautiful place, but the rivers and harbours are being polluted due to a lack of investment in the sewerage system and Government weakness on holding polluters to account. Too many properties sold for holidays homes is hollowing out communities and Lib Dems have plans to protect new homes so they can be occupied by full-time residents and ensure that second homeowners pay their fair share. In Mid Dorset and North Poole only the Liberal Democrats can beat the Conservatives, a vote for anyone else will give us another 5 years of the same decline. Dorset deserves better and I am ready to serve the residents, businesses and communities here fighting for a fair deal.

Susan Murray is the Liberal Democrat candidate for Mid Dunbartonshire. A current local councillor for Kirkintilloch East and North and Twechar, Susan is a strong, local and hardworking campaigner and has the experience that will deliver the change we need.

Too many MPs are career politicians with no understanding of life in the real world. She is a successful businesswoman who lives locally and will use here experience getting things done as an East Dunbartonshire councillor to deliver on the issues that matter most to residents.

For Susan, improving local healthcare is a personal priority. When her husband suffered a stroke, she became a carer. Her experience means Susan knows just how important it is to have good quality NHS facilities in our community, like the new Milngavie health and care centre she is campaigning for.

In Midlothian there are 2,446 children living in poverty. That's 2,446 childhoods I'm dedicating myself to changing. As an Executive Director at one of the world's biggest children's charities I lead a team of 160 to deliver award-winning campaigns and our programmes supporting families here in Scotland and across the UK.

I absolutely love my job but there's nothing I can do in it that will ever make as big a difference to our communities as Labour in government does. That's what's brought me back from community work to politics.

I was proud to work as a Downing Street adviser to Gordon Brown during the financial crisis, translating action at the G20 right down to where it made a difference, in protecting people's pensions, jobs, savings and homes.

Now I'm the chair of the advisory board for Our Scottish Future, giving a voice to everyone who wants to keep our country together but wants -- and needs -- change. I also volunteer on the boards of IPPR, The Center for Countering Digital Hate, The Labour Climate and Environment Forum, Larger Us, The Civic Power Fund and The Climate Coalition. The thing that brings all of this together is my belief that it doesn't have to be like this: that if we focus on what unites us we can meet and master the great challenges of the day. We have the chance to draw a line under the division and distraction of the past - and to inspire the Scottish people with the kind of future we will build together.

A Scottish decade where we have good green jobs, modern manufacturing and where talent - not class - determines what happens in the classroom. A future where we see growth not just in our economy but in our ambitions - where we create a Scotland where no child is hungry, no family is cold and each generation does better than the last. That's what we're fighting for - that's what's on the ballot paper at the general election. I'd love for you to be part of it. Please get in touch and let's get started.

Emily Darlington is Labour's Parliamentary Candidate for Milton Keynes Central. She has been delivering for MK as a councillor for many years including the biggest council house building programme for a generation, enhancing the biodiversity, striving towards a Dementia Friendly City and tackling violence towards women and girls by leading the White Ribbon City ambition. She lives in Milton Keynes with her husband and two children.

Milton Keynes is where I was born, went to school in, started my first job, and where my family still live and works today. However, in its near 60-year history, it has never had an MP who grew up here.

Instead, for the last 14 years, it has been served by Tory MPs who have let the city down and refused to fight for our local area. I will be an MP who fights for our city.

This is personal to me -- my family work in our local public services, my mum as a teacher and my brother as a firefighter. I've seen first-hand how more than a decade of Tory policy has undermined their craft and the services they provide. But in order to improve things we need a Labour government, and that won't happen unless we win in marginal seats like Milton Keynes North.

So get involved, because together we can win for Milton Keynes, and we can win for Labour.

I am standing as Labour's candidate at the next general election as I want to reverse the damage the Tories have done.

We all know there are huge challenges ahead - kick-starting the economy, supporting residents through the cost of living crisis and combatting the climate and nature emergencies.

But I am ready for that challenge. 

Monmouthshire needs someone who can make tough decisions to fix the chaos caused by the Tories over the past 13 years, and someone who will stand up in the House of Commons to strongly and proudly represent this beautiful area we call home.

I've lived in Monmouthshire for over 22 years and been active in the community ever since I moved here. For example,  I'm a governor at Monmouth Comprehensive where my son is at school. 

I'm an elected County Councillor, so I know how to make tough decisions.

As your MP, I will be your champion.  I'm driven and focused and I have a track record of delivering for those that need it most. For example, our first act as a new administration was ensuring that Welsh Government's cost of living funding was provided directly to those on the lowest incomes. 

Previously, as Chief Executive of a charity which fights for fairness, I turned it around in the six years I was there. I doubled the funding and grew the organisation's impact. I know how to influence government and have won important campaigns.

Together, it's time to build a fairer, greener more dynamic Monmouthshire constituency.

For 14 years, almost everything in our country has gone backwards. Waiting lists are at record highs. So is the tax burden. Crime, child poverty, and homelessness are all rising. We have become less prosperous compared to other major economies. Court backlogs and a lack of investment in prisons means our justice system is on its knees. The same is true for most public services, not least our buckling National Health Service.

Five Tory prime ministers have given us austerity, a cost-of-living crisis, a stagnant economy, and international isolation. They are not a serious party of government and we cannot risk another five years of Tory chaos.

My whole life is in this constituency. I teach its amazingly bright and talented children and raise my own in Acrefair. We have so much going for us, whether it is Ruabon’s proud industrial heritage, the grandeur of Powis and Chirk castles, Machynlleth’s art, festivals, and culture, or Rhosllanerchrugog’s strong vibrant Welsh community.

This election will be the first contested under new constituency boundaries, which have completely changed the political landscape here. The Liberal Democrats may in the past have been the traditional alternative to the Tories in Montgomeryshire, but with the addition of 13 Labour-voting wards in the north of our new constituency, on top of their plummeting vote share since 2010, this is simply no longer the case – a vote for them is now a vote to let the Tories sneak back in.

Montgomeryshire & Glyndŵr deserves so much better. Tory economic incompetence has decimated public finances and our local economies. Mid Wales has lost its Air Ambulance base. Welshpool had no banking access whatsoever for a whole year. There is still no health hub in Newtown.

For a region so dependent on reliable transport links, this Tory decline has hit us particularly hard. Rural bus services have halved in the past decade and a half. For Llanidloes, the only large town in Montgomeryshire without a train station, this causes pointless delays with the bus to Caersws missing connecting trains by minutes.

I am unashamedly proud of our farmers, who do so much for our local economy. Here again, Tory incompetence has hit us where it hurts, with Boris Johnson’s disastrous trade deal with Australia selling out the farming community. His successor as prime minister, Liz Truss, said he had “conceded the whole kingdom” with the deal. We welcome the news that rural voters are increasingly considering voting Labour. We will not take your support for granted and will support Welsh farmers by reducing the reliance on imported food and by cutting red tape at the border.

Labour has brought Britain back from the brink before. We will do so again. With Labour governments in Westminster, Cardiff Bay, and with a Labour MP in Montgomeryshire & Glyndŵr, we will work together to bring about a decade of renewal.

I will be a loud voice in Westminster for properly funding public services, most importantly our NHS. I will support restrictions on shameful corporate lobbying and back Labour’s plans to abolish the House of Lords. As a trade unionist since age 19 and current executive member of my trade union, I will back public sector workers to the hilt and stand up for workers’ rights. I fully support the creation of Great British Energy and the nationalisation of our railways, which I will leverage to bring cheap, clean energy and more reliable train services into our communities. I will call for an ambitious Green New Deal and make sure we protect our party democracy. I will work with MPs of any stripe in Dwyfor Meirionnydd, Radnorshire, Wrexham, Shropshire and Ludlow to keep our communities connected and drive the growth of our local economies.

Polls are showing a very close race between Labour and the Tories. If you are a Lib Dem, Plaid, or Green voter, we need you to lend us your vote so we can send a clear message to Rishi Sunak, who’s parliamentary private secretary is our very own Tory MP Craig Williams. He and his colleagues have taken rural, traditional areas like ours for granted. 14 years later and we desperately need change. A vote for Labour is a vote for that change.

From Rhos and Ruabon to Llanfyllin and Llangurig, in Chirk, Cefn, Welshpool, Machynlleth, and everywhere inbetween, I will be an MP for all of Montgomeryshire & Glyndŵr. I will fight tirelessly to secure our place in a more prosperous, safer, and greener Wales.

Graham studied Engineering at Strathclyde University and later through the Open University he gained a Diploma in Computing.Graham has worked as a storeman, then as a shift supervisor in retail before starting work with the SNP as a Parliamentary Assistant. Gaining experience in a parliamentary office he became a Constituency Office Manager and gained extensive experience working for a broad range of constituents’ interests and concerns with public, private and third sector organisations.Elected as a Councillor to serve Elgin City South in 2007 he continues to serve as a councillor for that area. He recently served as Leader of Moray Council for 4 years, during which he led on several budgets that got the Council into a much improved financial position, as well as Leading the Council through the challenges of the Covid Pandemic.The Administration he led introduced the Council’s Climate Change Strategy, putting in place an expert team to deliver it, and a new anti-poverty strategy; as well as tackling the challenges thrown up by the Covid pandemic.He is currently Co-Leader of the Moray SNP Council Group, the main Council opposition group and also serves as Chair of Moray Economic Partnership and Chair of the regional Space Leadership Group.Graham has a strong interest in Cost of Living issues, Economic Development & Renewable Energy.Away from work he enjoys spending time with his wife Louise - often at rock gigs and quiz nights - watching sport and playing the accordion.

Lizzi Collinge is the candidate for the new Morecambe and Lunesdale constituency, having been selected by local members in September 2023. Lizzi was born near Blackburn but grew up in a small village in Cumbria. She moved to the area in 2005 and now lives in Heysham with her husband and two kids.

A project manager by trade, Lizzi is an experienced representative having been elected to Lancashire County Council in 2016 where she now serves as Shadow Cabinet Member for Health and Wellbeing. Lizzi is also the Deputy Chair of Lancashire Health and Adult Services Scrutiny Committee. She is passionate about health and ensuring that health is considered in all areas of policy.

With a reputation for empathy, hard work and tenacity, Lizzi enjoys widespread support across the new constituency. After her selection Lizzi said: "I hope to win people's trust to represent them in Westminster and to help deliver the change our country so desperately needs. People are fed up of public services that are run into the ground and an economy that doesn't work for them, especially when the Government doesn't seem to care about basic decency and honesty. People have been badly let down.

"People in Morecambe and Lunesdale deserve an MP who will fight their corner and I plan to be a great constituency MP."

In her spare time Lizzi is a keen gardener, growing her own fruit and veg and making her own preserves.

Islanders feel they have been taken for granted for too long. Na h-Eileanan an Iar constituency has been ignored by an uncaring Tory government which fuelled the cost-of-living crisis and neglected by an SNP government whose incompetence handled us a ferry crisis, a housing crisis and the danger of depopulation.



We have come to a crossroads where we can shape our own future as a vibrant island communities, tapping into the support of a change-making Labour government, or we can slip back into further division under Tory and nationalist rule.



I grew up in Lewis and know all the islands well from my work as a newspaper reporter and programme maker for the BBC. As a journalist in Westminster for many years I have seen politics close up.



I don't need a map of the Hebrides or the House of Commons to tell me only Labour can bring about the economic and democratic renewal the country and the islands demand.



As a Labour MP I will shape policy for the islands and speak up for the islands. We face a big challenge but Na h-Eileanan an Iar has been Labour seat before and can be again. With your support we will win here, we will see a Labour government, we will raise a new voice for the islands.

Lee has lived in West Berkshire all his life. 'My wife and I both work in the local area, and our children go to local schools. We access the same services, local doctors, schools and public transport as you, and like you, we demand better from our government on the issues we all face locally and nationally. I want to see a West Berkshire that is confident for a brighter future, which is why I invite you to join me in demanding better.'

Lee became politically motivated to join the local Liberal Democrats in 1999 at the age of 16 when David Rendel was MP for Newbury. Personally seeing the positive differences that were made to the local community, Lee was inspired to become a councillor in Thatcham in 2007. Since then, he has been Mayor twice, Leader of Thatcham Town Council, and is currently the Leader of the Opposition on West Berkshire Council fighting for a better deal from central government to help fund our vital local services.

With a proven track record of standing up for residents, Lee continues to hold the Tories to account. ‘Our District has missed out on much need affordable housing and we have unnecessarily lost many community assets including Newbury football Club. We have also seen hundreds of thousands of pounds of taxpayers money being wasted defending incompetent decisions in court.’

With continued and significant electoral success for West Berkshire and Newbury Liberal Democrats, Lee and the Liberal Democrats are standing up for voters on important areas such as housing, education and the environment. Under Lee’s leadership they won widespread support from the people of West Berkshire, increasing their representation on West Berkshire Council almost fourfold and regained control of both Newbury and Thatcham town councils. 

Lee is committed to the community and people of West Berkshire and continues to stand up for our area. Your support can make the difference in giving West Berkshire a hardworking, committed local MP that will work for you.

Lee Dillon - a better future for West Berkshire.

My name is Adam Jogee: your Labour Candidate for Newcastle-under-Lyme I am honoured to be Labour's candidate for the next Member of Parliament for Newcastle-under-Lyme. My values are Staffordshire values: hard work, common sense, and decency. These values shaped my family and drive me every day.​

I am resilient, committed, and focused. I will lead by example. I don't want just to be an MP; I want to be your MP here in Newcastle-under-Lyme.

Newcastle-under-Lyme has been let down and left behind by 14 years of Conservative government. The cost of living crisis has made life tough for people across our area, crime is on the rise, and our NHS is broken.

My wife is an ICU nurse in our NHS, so I understand the pressures the health service is facing, seeing the impact of the Tories' failure to manage the NHS effectively. In my day job in Labour's Environment team I've worked on Walleys Quarry and raised it at a national level. I am well placed to tackle the issue with both hands, rolling my sleeves up to get the answers and action you deserve.

As your MP, I will fight to cut your energy bills, grow our economy, rebuild community policing to tackle antisocial behaviour, reduce NHS waiting times, break down barriers to opportunity by recruiting more teachers and expanding apprenticeships, and protect our environment by cleaning our air and addressing the issue of Walleys Quarry.

In me, you will have a dedicated MP. I will work hard, engage with you, and be present. I will work day in and day out to earn your trust and support.

​Newcastle-under-Lyme deserves change. It deserves a fresh start and a mission-driven government that will restore pride and purpose to our country.

 I will deliver that change.

statement_to_voters:
I am seeking re-election for Newcastle Central. I was born in Wallsend, grew up in North Kenton and live in Newcastle Central. I have been immensely proud to represent my city and to stand up in Parliament for the interests of the people I grew up with. Helping my constituents has been my primary aim and each month I publish on my website summaries of the casework I and my team have dealt with (www.chionwurahmp.com) I am particularly proud of the work I did to keep the Richardson Unit open at the RVI, and also campaigning against Wonga sponsoring Newcastle United, part of a process that led to

these companies being properly regulated.

As a Chartered Engineer, I am passionate about the difference technology can make to people's lives -- with the right Government! As Shadow Minister for Industrial Strategy, Science and Innovation I have worked with colleagues to develop policies for a Green Industrial Revolution, which will bring thousands of jobs to Newcastle and the North East building on our proud tradition of manufacturing.

I want to continue this work, and move the centre of gravity of our industry and prosperity Northwards. We need to resolve this Brexit crisis, but for the country not for the rich, with people having the final say. We need a Green Industrial Revolution, to rebuild the country after a decade of austerity, and to protect our vital public services.

statement_to_voters: I was born and brought up in Newport West, it is the place I still call home. I will continue to work with local people to put our city first, standing up for Newport West in Westminster.

I'm proud to be running to represent our community as a Labour Member of Parliament. The newly created Newton Aycliffe and Spennymoor constituency is my home. I was born, raised and live in Aycliffe, Mam trained at Aycliffe Hospital, Dad went to school in Ferryhill and my Grandad grew up in Trimdon.



I've dedicated my career to making a difference and have a track record of making things happen. I have professional experience of managing large teams and budgets as a housing association director, helping to build genuinely affordable homes. As a senior leader in a large local authority, I delivered major regeneration projects which brought jobs, homes and community facilities.



It would be a huge honour to be able to use my skills and experience to be the powerful voice our area deserves in Westminster.

Lucy grew up near Northampton and she is Labour's parliamentary candidate for Northampton North. Lucy is determined to secure a Labour Government that delivers jobs, investment and the quality public services that the town deserves, and that Britain so desperately needs.

Lucy is a competition lawyer and a partner in London firm Hausfeld & Co LLP. She has previously worked for Slaughter and May, the Office of Fair Trading, Which? and the United Nations Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia. Lucy is listed in the Legal 500 as ""an outstanding junior partner"" and regularly speaks at conferences regarding competition law and collective redress. Lucy is passionate about access to justice and she has been involved in the development of a number of law centres. She currently serves on the board of the Collective Redress Lawyers Association.

Mike Reader is your parliamentary candidate for the next general election. Mike has a vision for Northampton - to make it greener, more prosperous and fairer. Mike brings over fifteen years of experience working in the construction industry to bear as your parliamentary candidate, skilled in bringing different parties together to solve seemingly impossible problems, creating new jobs and business opportunities for small and medium sized businesses. He currently leads a team at an international consultancy and construction firm who design and implement campaigns to help governments achieve best value from their construction and infrastructure projects across the globe, from new railways in Canada to schools in Australia, to regeneration programmes in Greece.

Mike is internationally recognised as a leader in his field, having been named UK Young Achiever of the Year by Constructing Excellence in 2016 and a Global 40 under 40 leader by the APMP in 2020, as well as receiving the International Award for Excellence in 2022 from industry peers.

As a passionate campaigner and environmentalist, Mike is determined to bring new green jobs to Northampton, clean up our streets and solve the air pollution crisis in the town.

Mike lives in Northampton, and as a local resident, is an active member of our community, already helping to make the town better.

I am determined to be North Cornwall’s loud voice in Westminster instead of a Tory cheerleader who refuses to speak up for us in Parliament. After 14 years of failure and neglect by the Tories we need a fresh start. The Liberal Democrats are the only party that can win here in North Cornwall and deliver the fresh ideas our area urgently needs.

It is time to stand up and fight for North Cornwall and that is what I will do. If you want to see real change for our area, I urge you to get in touch and get involved with my campaign.

We all know that the next general election is going to be crucial for our country. So it’s an honour for me to have been chosen as the Liberal Democrat candidate for North Devon. I love this area and feel lucky to have brought up my family here after being posted to Chivenor by the RAF in 1989. I’m a bluff Yorkshireman who has made Barnstaple my home for the last 34 years, during which time I’ve served my community through work, local politics and fundraising.

I came here by chance but I’ve stayed here by choice.

I’m hoping to represent the people of North Devon in Westminster and to make their voices heard. Having worked in healthcare and housing, I understand the pressures that people face.

I have served the community in my charity work and in Barnstaple by being an elected councillor, at town, district and county level. I see North Devon is facing enormous challenges and we are currently being let down, due to the cost of living crisis, the lack of political action to protect our environment and the shortage of affordable housing and opportunities. We need better paid jobs and the right training for our young people.

According to a recent social mobility report from Exeter University, there is an absence of a strong political voice at the national level advocating on behalf of the region, unlike, for example, the Northern Powerhouse movement. Instead, politicians here believe things are “fine”. I want to challenge this and ensure that I am North Devon’s voice in Parliament and not Parliament’s voice in North Devon.

Housing is something I feel passionately about, and it’s one where the people of North Devon are being let down, victims of the rising market for second homes and holiday lets. Second homes have left some coastal villages such as Croyde, Mortehoe and Georgeham like ghost towns in the winter, but full to bursting in the summer.

I pledge a sincere commitment to serve the constituency of North Devon, the place my children were born and the area I love.

I want to take the leadership skills, experience and courage I have shown in 36 years of political life, and use them to follow Kevan Jones as a strong Labour voice for North Durham.

I have been a Labour Party member since 1988, serving at every level from the grassroots up, through 12 years as a councillor, standing for parliament in Tory seats in 2001 and 2005, to a total of 6 years on the National Executive Committee, where I have played a leading role in turning Labour back into a winning party. I am 52, married with sons aged 12 and 18. I overcame a very serious neurological disease, which left me unable to walk for a year, and resultant disability, to become a very active Labour campaigner again. This has made me an even more passionate champion of the NHS. I also care deeply about tackling poverty and inequality and have professional experience of fighting for inward investment and strong regional industrial policies.

I have always believed in the importance of public service, that contributing to the greater good uplifts both ourselves and our communities. It's what motivated me to join the Army: the chance to do something for my country.



But incredibly, even as I deployed to Afghanistan, I saw the military being hollowed out around me under the Conservatives' disastrous austerity policies.



It's the same story all around us with our other public services. When I'm speaking to voters on the doorsteps in North East Derbyshire, they're telling me that they can't get an NHS dentist appointment. That they can't rely on their local bus. And that they're worried about this week's food shop.



Well this isn't the country I want. I know it's not what you want. That's why I'm standing for Labour because I know that we can be better, and get our future back.

Originally from Greenock, Wendy has lived in Fife since 2003 with her husband and two children.

Following her degree in English from Edinburgh University, Wendy joined Lothian and Borders Police in 1999, serving for 12 years as a Police officer. After a period in a variety of operational policing roles, she moved into HR and Learning and Development, during which time she worked for the Association of Chief Police Officers in Scotland and in the Business Management Unit of the Scottish Police College. During this period she also worked part-time as a Communications Lecturer for the then Lauder College (now Fife College) in Dunfermline.

She left the Police in 2011 and following a career break to look after her young children, joined the MoD contractor, Right Management, working at MoD Caledonia, Rosyth, as the Scottish Regional Employment and Training Manager on their military resettlement contract, supporting service veterans into positive employment outcomes.

In October 2015, she commenced employment as a Capability and Development Manager with a global drinks manufacturer. Always engaged in her local community, she has held committee roles on a variety of parent bodies and became the first female Board Member of the Camanachd Association (the governing body for the amateur sport of shinty) in 2017.

She grew up in a Liberal tradition, with an Argyllshire grandfather who knew both Ray Michie and Jo Grimond. She joined the Scottish Liberal Democrats in May 2015.

Having stood as both a Council and General Election candidate in 2017, she was selected as the Westminster Prospective Parliamentary candidate for the constituency of North East Fife in June 2018. She was elected to Parliament in the 2019 General Election.

I am a charity leader in North East Hampshire ready to offer our beautiful area of the country a better alternative at the next general election. I strongly believe our home needs an MP who can represent the interests of everyone... someone with experience of real life outside of politics.  People tell me they want a hard-working, visible, local MP. I can promise that's exactly what I'll be.

Chris lives in North East Herts, in Royston. He is a local District Councillor and already has experience representing the local community on issues from NHS services to banking hubs. Chris worked for the Campaign to Protect Rural England for the previous 5 years, championing the needs of towns and villages like those in North East Herts.

Dan Norris loves our part of the world. He has lived, worked and served here for decades including as our Mayor and local MP. He previously worked across the area as an NSPCC trained child protection officer as well as running his own business. For the last thirty years Dan’s home has been near Pensford. He and his cocker spaniel Angel, love taking walks in the area. Dan supports Bristol City whose ups and downs have been the perfect training for politics. He is an animal welfare champion who wants to see the loopholes in the Hunting Act closed. His deep local roots means he knows where we live is a unique and wholly special place. Dan is very proud and hugely ambitious for our area.   Dan Norris CV    Labour General Election candidate. Fighting to get Britain’s future back.   Mayor 2021 – Present  Bringing record sums of investment to our area. Giving you free travel throughout your Birthday month. Planting the biggest wood in the West and wildflower meadows including in Jubilee Park.    MP 1997– 2010  Voting for the minimum wage, bringing down waiting lists and introducing Sure Start. Assisting in the Northern Ireland Peace talks.   Government Environment Minister. When we had the cleanest rivers, beaches, drinking water and air since before the industrial revolution.   NSPCC trained child protection officer. Seeing society at its worst and best.

“I’m pleased to see that the Prime Minister has finally found the guts to ask the country what it thinks about years of Conservative failure in Government. Our NHS waiting lists have spiralled, our precious coastline is polluted, and public services are cracking under the pressure of chronic underfunding. 

“I’ve spoken to thousands of people across North Norfolk over the past few months, and what has become clear is that they are fed up with the contempt that the Conservative government and our Conservative MP have treated them with.

“I’m delighted that we will have the opportunity to put forward the positive Liberal Democrat vision for the country. We will guarantee people the right to see their GP, and end the 8am rush. 

“We’re going to ensure people receive timely treatment for cancer, and ensure investment in research to bring about new tests and treatments for some of the toughest cancers. 

“We’re going to recruit more dentists, fix the NHS dentistry crisis and stop North Norfolk being a dental desert.

“North Norfolk deserves an MP with the courage of their convictions, who will speak up for them and vote in their interests, not simply follow the party line. We need a strong voice to bring about a new kind of politics. 

“I’m excited to spend the next 6 weeks speaking to people across our area and hearing from them how we can bring about the real change we desperately need. It’s time for a fair deal for North Norfolk, and that comes by voting for the Liberal Democrats.”

As an award-winning local pharmacist and former councillor, I am committed to serving the community.

My two children are the reason I got into politics, to fight for a future in which they and all people in North Somerset have the opportunity to thrive.

I live in Bristol and am house hunting right now in Portishead.

As a healthcare professional, I will prioritise rebuilding our NHS and a country of which we can all be proud. People in North Somerset deserve better.

I am ready to deliver the change we need.

I'm Rachel Taylor a local property solicitor, born and raised in the constituency with a passion for delivering the change we need here in North Warwickshire and Bedworth, with the experience, confidence and dedication to get the job done.



I believe in the potential of our area, I already work with businesses across our region to grow, create jobs and regenerate our area and I will work hard to deliver a better future for North Warwickshire and Bedworth. That means good schools for all our children, access to vital health and social care when we need it, better training and apprenticeships, investment in green energy and food production, a healthy and stable economy creating good jobs and opportunities for business, an end to water companies polluting our rivers with sewage, public transport back under public control delivering vital routes for our rural communities and a government that is on your side working for everyone not one that leaves you feeling less safe or struggling to make ends meet and worried about the future.



As a Wimbledon Tennis Umpire I was used to making the right calls under pressure, as a solicitor I work hard to deliver the best for my clients and uphold the highest standards, as a charity manager I delivered vital funding to those who needed it most, as a local councillor I stand up for local people and fight for local services.



I am meeting thousands of local people and listening to your concerns so that I can deliver what matters to you after the next General Election. North Warwickshire and Bedworth deserves an MP that is visible, hard working and who can bring national experience and local knowledge to secure the future we need. I am ready for the challenge and I will work hard for you.

I grew up in a deprived rural area, and entered politics to fight for a real alternative to the Tories' national decline - with shops closing, more families struggling, and healthcare services crumbling.



Whether living in the most rural parts of North West Cambridgeshire, or in our towns, or in the southern half of Peterborough - people of all ages across our constituency are witnessing a continual decline in public services. GP appointments are impossible to access, local bus services continue to be cut, and there is a desperate lack of affordable housing across our area -- from Ramsey to Wittering and everywhere in between.



Only a Labour government can deliver the change that North West Cambridgeshire needs. I will stand up for our communities, and I am delighted to advocate for a Labour government to restore hope and opportunity across our area.



My background is in biomedical research, and I strongly believe that we need more scientists in Parliament - as well as more young people with real-world experience of the issues that our country is grappling with. I also have experience as a district councillor, where I am working to protect and enhance local government services despite the precarious financial circumstances the government has left councils in across Britain. I'm an experienced representative with a record of delivery, and I hope to gain the trust of North West Cambridgeshire's residents to deliver real change for our communities.

Kemi Badenoch has served as the MP for the Saffron Walden constituency since 2017, having been re-selected in 2019. Kemi is now the Conservative candidate for North West Essex.

Kemi is currently Secretary of State for Business and Trade, President of the Board of Trade and Minister for Women and Equalities.

She has previously held roles as Minister for Local Government, Faith and Communities at the Department of Levelling Up, Housing and Communities, Minister for Equalities, Exchequer Secretary to the Treasury and Parliamentary Under Secretary of State at the Department for Education.

Kemi is a former Vice-Chair of the Conservative Party and former member of the Justice Select Committee. Prior to her election as a Member of Parliament, she was a Conservative member of the London Assembly, acting as the GLA Conservative’s spokesperson for the economy.

She other areas of interest include engineering and technology, social mobility and integration. She provides regular mentoring to women who wish to pursue careers in technology.

Kemi has supported hundreds of people across the Saffron Walden constituency with a wide range of individual issues, community and national concerns. She works closely with the local councils, schools, businesses, community groups and many more to represent the interests of her constituents and their communities.

Four and a half years ago I had the honour to be elected to represent North West Norfolk and now I am campaigning to be re-elected to ensure we have a new QEH by 2030, deliver £70 m of projects in Lynn, stronger economy, better transport links, fight crime, protect the environment, invest in defence, and more.

I couldn't be prouder to be from Norfolk. I grew up in one of the county's small villages and went to the local comprehensive school. Norwich is my home and I know what a brilliant place it is. But our community has been let down, just as the country has.

I've been lucky enough to have a good state education, a good job and good health. Everyone deserves those things in a prosperous society. This isn't the reality in Norwich North under the Tories. Many people simply don't feel better off after over a decade of Conservative Government.

Throughout my life I've stood up for hope -- for fairness, for dignity, for equality. I've spent most of my career in the charity sector where I've campaigned for children's rights, against hunger, poverty and inequality. Wherever, I've lived I've been active in my community -- I've been a Labour councillor, a school governor, a Hospital Trust governor and during Covid I volunteered at a food bank delivering parcels.

Since becoming your candidate, I've spoken to thousands of you, listening to your experience under this Government and the change you want to see. With people right across our area, I've already fought to save our NHS walk-in centre, shone a spotlight on the state of our buses and backed our local businesses.

I will always be on your side. I want to use my skills, and experience to restore trust, hope and opportunity for everyone in Norwich North.

If you live in Norwich North and have any questions or thoughts please do get in touch.

I’ve lived in Norwich since 2001 and been your MP for the last two years, so I know exactly what a special place this is. 

We’re a city that’s proud of standing out and doing things differently. While Norfolk is a sea of blue, we don’t have a single Tory councillor in Norwich. While the country voted to leave the EU, Norwich South voted 60:40 to remain. But above all, we’re a live-and-let-live city that’s united by our sense of fairness and which truly values all of our public services -  from our NHS through our fantastic local Police and Fire Service to the many hundreds of wonderful staff who care for our city’s older people.

As your MP I’ve taken action for Norwich on all of these issues and many more. I’ve opposed this government’s ruinous, self serving and ideological cuts to our local health service and social care system. I’ve stood up for our city’s parents and pupils as Tory school funding plans hit our schools far harder than anywhere else in East Anglia. Theresa May’s obsession with Brexit at all costs will hit Norwich hard, so I took a principled stand for our city against it in Parliament which meant I had to resign from my role as Shadow Secretary for Business. 

And because I know that so many in our city are working hard and still struggling to make ends meet, I am donating almost all of my MP’s 10% payrise to local charities.

"I am Jodie Gosling and I am standing for re-election to continue my role as your Borough Council. I’ve lived in New Arley for 10 years with my partner and three children. I have been so proud to represent Oldham East and Saddleworth since 2011, during which time I have dealt with 33,000 local cases.

My award winning Be Fair - Pay on Time campaign started as a local issue but became a national campaign. Recommendations from my parliamentary inquiry were incorporated into 2014 Small Business Act and late payments to small businesses have fallen from £41.5bn in 2014 to £14bn now.

With over 2,000 people across the constituency living with dementia, my Dementia Friendly Oldham campaign has created over 8,500 Dementia Friends. I will continue to fight for the rights of disabled people, including those with dementia, influencing attitudes and changing practices.

Since 2014 my annual summer school has brought scores of young people from across Oldham borough together, to empower them, and to raise their awareness about what politics is all about: public service.

I will continue to fight for improved access at Greenfield station, reliable and affordable bus services and forfunding to fix our brownfield sites, so we always build on brownfield sites first, tackling the housing shortage while protecting our green spaces.

If re-elected I promise to continue to work as hard as I can for you, providing a strong, experienced voice in Parliament and making a real difference for residents and businesses in Oldham East and Saddleworth.

Being the Labour & Co-Operative MP for Oldham West and Royton since 2015 has been a huge privilege for me, but the job is far from over. We need a Labour government to rebuild Britain, invest in our public services and stitch back together the fabric of our public realm.

If re-elected I will ensure Chadderton, Oldham and Royton have a voice on the national stage, and continue to campaign for the issues that matter to local people, like supporting WASPI women mistreated by the Tories, fighting for those affected by the contaminated blood scandal, fighting for the over-75's to keep their free TV licenses and for Universal Credit to be scrapped.

Alistair was elected to Parliament in 2001 as MP for Orkney and Shetland.

Alistair was born and raised on Islay. He first worked in the hotel industry before attending University of Aberdeen where he graduated with a degree in Law in 1992. After graduating, Alistair worked as a Procurator Fiscal Depute then moved into private practise as a solicitor.

He married his wife Kate in 1987 and they live in Orkney with their two sons, Sandy and Simon.

Since becoming an MP in 2001, Alistair has campaigned on a range of issues important to people in the Northern Isles, such as farming, fishing, offshore oil and gas, and more recently the development of renewables. He is also well-known for his work on human rights and has been an active campaigner for the worldwide abolition of the death penalty.

Raised in Wakefield, I'm the product of a hardworking family committed to public service.​

My mum is a carer and my dad is a prison officer.

I've faced many of the same struggles that people across our area face daily - and I've used these experiences to fight for what is best for people locally throughout my career.

Unlike many in politics, I didn't take the typical path through university. I haven't got a degree and I haven't spent a lot of time in the Halls of Westminster.

Instead, my career began locally. I got my first job aged 13. My first proper job was at River Island in the Ridings in Wakefield, when I was 16 - and then as a Community Development Officer working with local kids at Wakefield Trinity, where I secured funding to improve local children's health and wellbeing, and giving 2,000 young people the chance to engage with sport.

Now, in my professional life, I work to support vital local and national campaigns, like holding water companies to account when they pollute our rivers and seas, calling for support through the cost of living crisis and tackling NHS waiting lists.

These are all key issues facing us across Ossett and Denby Dale.

In the last four years, Labour has changed. And whilst we've changed for the better, the Conservatives have changed Britain for the worse.

We all know the damage that the Conservatives have done over the last 13 years. And we all know that we can't afford any more.

​That's why I am standing - because I believe we deserve better. Because it's time for change. Because we deserve a fresh start.

Since leaving the police service, I have been an active campaigner across Pendle and Ribble Valley, being a key member of the Ribble Valley Labour team which secured our best ever result in the 2023 local elections.
