statement_to_voters:
I am delighted to announce that I have been selected as the Labour party candidate for North Swindon in the next general election. It is a tremendous honour to have the opportunity to represent the town where I was born and raised.

Swindon is a great town and deserves an MP who will represent it with pride and put the residents first.

I already have the privilege of being a borough councillor in Swindon. I am also a local business owner and an armed forces veteran.

Swindon is my home. I was born here, went to school at what used to be Churchfields and now live in Old Town with my husband, Martin. Having previously served as the Labour MP for Lewisham East and as London's Deputy Mayor for Transport, I want to use my skills and experience to make a difference in my home town. Swindon is crying out for investment and people need real help with the soaring cost of living. We need better quality jobs available locally, a town centre we can be proud of, schools that nurture children's interest in the world around them and an NHS fit for the challenges of the 21st century. It would be an honour to represent my home town in Parliament. If you live in Swindon South and have any questions or if you would just like to say hello, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

I would be a strong MP opposing the Conservatives’ cuts to almost every local school, who will fight the closure of our Norton Manor Camp and speak up for public service, and who will stand for a better world for our children and young people, giving them a stake in the future of our country.

The Conservatives’ chopping the LibDems’ guaranteed annual 2.5% pension increase is also wrong, and their ‘tax’ on the cost of care will mean people will have to give up the value of their home if they suffer from long term conditions like dementia. This is the new hardline Conservative Party and we need an MP to stand up to it – that is my promise to you. I have had my own career and have no interest in the Ministerial greasy pole, my offer is to stand up for you and everyone across this constituency without fear or favour. As more and more of my posters go up people are now flocking to my campaign.  Whichever way they voted in the referendum people know he dangers of the extreme Theresa May/Nigel Farage approach antagonises neighbouring countries. You know that crashing out without a deal would be a serious disaster for trade, jobs and prices right here where we live. I want us to unite around protecting the best of our links abroad. People don’t want to write any Party a blank cheque in this election and know the wisdom of the final deal in two years’ time being subject to a vote by the people, especially by our young people whose lives will be most affected by it.

I will stand up for you against the Government whenever they get things wrong. On protecting our incomes and jobs, our precious environment, our pensions and our care in later life, the Conservatives must not be allowed to make you suffer. We need a strong MP to take them on when it matters, to give opportunities to younger people and secure a better future for our area here in Somerset where I grew up. I will be that strong MP.   Published & Promoted by J Fulljames on behalf of Gideon Amos (Liberal Democrats) 83 Staplegrove Road Taunton TA1 1DN.

Hello, 

I’m Cameron Thomas and I'm your Liberal Democrat Parliamentary Candidate in Tewkesbury Constituency. I first moved here following an assignment at Imjin Barracks in 2016, and settled with my family shortly afterward.

I'm not a career politician, I consider myself to be a public servant. 

I joined the RAF as a teenager in 2000 and served across the world prior to my resignation in 2023, so that I could stand to represent you. My specialisations were communications and information systems, policing and security, training and inclusion. I served on several operational deployments throughout my career, including 3 to Iraq, and to the Falkland Islands. One such deployment was an assignment to East Midlands NHS Trust, as a Military Planner to help issue Covid 19 Vaccines to thousands of residents across Leicestershire. I love and respect our NHS and will fight to protect it. It must be preserved so that help is there when we most need it. Doctors, nurses and staff must be supported and fairly paid.

I'm passionate about laying the foundations for young people to achieve their potential. Key to this is through a fair and well-funded education system; ours needs a complete overhaul and significant investment. It also means preserving our environment and increasing biodiversity. Nature is key to our mental health, and I want our children to enjoy the wealth of different species which we ourselves have enjoyed. I have been a marine conservation campaigner for 20 years and have joined and led expeditions in the Pacific Ocean, North Sea and English Channel. In our constituency, I have engaged with the Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust and look forward to helping them preserve our biodiversity from Westminster if elected.

As a retired Military Police Officer, I am your law and order candidate, but I am driven by compassion, empathy and public service. I will always speak out against injustice and defend others when they need it... it's in my DNA. I hope that my background will convince you that I'll represent you with courage and integrity, because I will. For too long, those who represent us have taken us for granted, voted against our interests, broken the rules they themselves implemented, and then lied to our faces about it. We deserve leaders who'll set a better example. That's why I'm standing.

At this General Election, it's the Liberal Democrats who are best placed to beat the Conservatives. I'd helped campaign with the Lib Dems at the previous election, in which we finished 2nd, some distance ahead of Labour. Since then, our constituency has benefitted by electing more Lib Dem District Councillors at Cheltenham Borough, Tewkesbury Borough and Gloucester City Councils than every other party combined. Our councillors lead all 3 of those councils, and are delivering for residents every day. I am absolutely convinced that the Liberal Democrats are a force for good in UK politics, and are the most environmentally conscious party in the country. I am so proud to stand as their candidate, for you. I am a candidate for our entire constituency, and have been campaigning from Twyning in the North, to Longford in the South, from Apperley in the West, to Winchcombe in the East.

If elected, I pledge to work cross-party to: ✅ Defend our NHS, ✅ Tackle the cost of living crisis, and ✅ Protect our Environment. The Lib Dems have already taken the lead on these issues, where other parties have followed.

Thank you so much for taking the time to read about me. You can find more information at my website here: cameronthomas.co.uk.

Please, for change in Tewkesbury, vote for Cameron Thomas and the Liberal Democrats on 4th July 2024.

Cameron Thomas - Standing up for you in Tewkesbury Constituency

I am a former civil servant who was born and brought up in Thurrock and I am now raising my family here. I am an unpaid carer for my daughter, a community volunteer and am a passionate campaigner for disability rights.

I am truly honoured to be Labour's candidate for my home here in Thurrock. Our community have been hit hard by the Tories failures. They've bankrupted our council, we have some of the worst GP waiting times in the country and some of the worst levels of air pollution outside of London. Everyone here is feeling the pinch of the cost of living crisis, while the Tory Government prioritise resolving their own internal squabbles over running the country.

I am determined to be a champion for Thurrock and for the people living here. I look forward to hearing from people in Thurrock what they want to see from a Labour Government and having conversations about how they will see a real positive change with Labour for both our community and our country.

For more than half my life, I’ve been lucky enough to call this new constituency my home. I spent my childhood in Taunton Deane and since 2006 my family and I have lived in Bampton, which I am proud to represent as Lib Dem district councillor.

I’ve visited every corner of the constituency, our towns and villages, our coast, countryside and moorland, and have a thorough understanding of our many strengths – and the challenges we face.

When it comes to my professional skills, my time as both a director of the NFU and head of strategy at the Environment Agency lend me crucial experience in our rural constituency, and my volunteer experience with the Exmoor Foundation for Integrated Health Care has given me invaluable insight into community health care.

As a politician and a working mother, I’ve mastered many important skills. I love the fun and camaraderie of the campaign trail, and know how to keep people’s spirits up. I always treat my opponents with courtesy and respect, and I’ve never been afraid of speaking truth to power. I have a thick skin, a warm heart and I’m absolutely passionate about bringing a visible local representation to my long-ignored community.

There is so much to be done in Truro and Falmouth, from working to build the green economy and create the jobs that Cornwall needs, to cleaning up our rivers and seas.

I live and work in the constituency having moved here 18 years ago when I married a naval pilot. Before that, I worked for a number of years as a solicitor representing working people who had accidents at work or employment claims.

As a single parent in Cornwall I put my legal skills to use at Cornwall Citizens Advice and then worked as a teaching assistant at Falmouth Secondary School for seven years while my son was in school.

I stood for Parliament for the first time in Truro and Falmouth in 2017 when we tripled the Labour vote here and made It a Conservative/Labour marginal constituency. I am now Labour Group Leader on Cornwall Council and also sit on Falmouth Town Council. Notable successes include proposing & pushing through Cornwall Council's Climate Emergency declaration, forcing a budget amendment to provide £3.5 million for mental healthcare for our young people in schools and shaping and campaigning on housing policy, which is such a vital issue in Cornwall.

My priorities for Truro and Falmouth are:

1\. The new Green Economy and decent, well-paid jobs that Cornwall needs and deserves.

2\. Tackling Cornwall's housing crisis.

3\. Saving and rebuilding Cornwall's NHS and social care.

I am working hard to be the next MP for Truro and Falmouth, so that I can be a strong and effective advocate for Cornwall in Westminster.

Munira Wilson is an experienced senior businesswoman with a professional, political and social track record, living in Whitton.

Munira has lived in Twickenham since 2005, and now lives with her husband and young family in Whitton. Munira is a former Twickenham councillor who helped to secure road safety improvements, tackle crime and anti-social behaviour and worked to protect the local environment.

Munira is campaigning to stop Brexit and for more investment in public services, including more funding for our schools and more police on our streets. She also believes we need urgent action to tackle the climate emergency which is threatening our very existence.

Locally, Munira will continue to champion local people’s concerns by opposing Conservative plans for a third runway at Heathrow and improving air quality, holding South Western Railway and Network Rail to account over poor service and inaccessible stations and helping to tackle the Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) funding crisis.

Munira currently works as Corporate Affairs Director for a science and technology company leading on Brexit and health policy for the last three years. She has previously worked for health and children’s charities, as well as the NHS, and holds a modern languages degree from Cambridge University.

Munira is proud to represent her home seat, which includes Twickenham, Teddington, the Hamptons, St Margarets and Whitton. Twickenham is always a straight fight between the Liberal Democrats and the Conservatives. Labour have not had a councillor elected for over 20 years and they've never had an MP here.

I was born at Hillingdon Hospital in 1988 -- growing up in South Ruislip and Ruislip Manor. I went to local schools. My family have called Uxbridge & South Ruislip their home for generations. I'm here, ready to work hard to improve the area who made me who I am today. Raised by a single parent, my life was shaped by early struggle and poverty. It was my first experience of homelessness, that drove me to join the Labour Party when I was a teenager. Losing our home, when I was 15, forced my mother and I to leave the area -- but Ruislip is where my roots are.

I believe everyone has a right to a decent home. No one should not be able to afford to eat or heat their home. More and more families are now struggling because of the Conservative government's economic mismanagement over the last 14 years. Now we need change. Over almost a decade I've put my principles into practice. Through my nine years as a local councillor and cabinet member I've been finding solutions to tackle low pay, deliver new council homes and good work.

Now, as times get even tougher for families, I am determined to make fundamental change possible in Parliament. As a full-time local MP, I would work hard for a new hospital and better public services. Work tirelessly to deliver a stable and growing economy so that families feel hopeful about the future and to ensure we have more police on the street and safer communities.

Diolch am ymweld. I'm Kanishka, Labour's Parliamentary Candidate in the Vale of Glamorgan.

I am a Barry resident, raised in Cardiff, who witnessed a Labour government's impact from Westminster firsthand: the dawn of a minimum wage, a boost in funding for education and healthcare, an economy going in the right direction.

Part of a new generation in politics, I am standing to undo the damage of thirteen years of Conservative government. My priorities are getting the basics right -- good local jobs, safer neighbourhoods, our community first. At its core, I believe that, together, we can make a brighter tomorrow for the Vale.

Ymunwch â mi!

If re-elected as your MP, I will fight for the change that Vauxhall and Camberwell Green needs. That means strong local services, thriving high streets, quality housing that is genuinely affordable for local people, stronger rights for renters, robust action on the climate emergency and a new deal for working people to ensure everyone enjoys the rights they deserve.   I will fight for the change people in our area need; safer streets, action on the climate emergency and quality affordable housing. I'm a proud South Londoner; I have lived in the area all my life and I was raised on a council estate in Brixton. I first stood for political office because I was sick of seeing life-changing decisions being made to my community and not by them. As the MP for Vauxhall since 2019 and the Assembly Member for Lambeth and Southwark prior to that, I will continue to make your voice heard in Parliament.

Simon Lightwood is the Labour MP for Wakefield. He was elected in the by-election held on, 23 June 2022 following the resignation of the disgraced Conservative MP Imran Ahmad Khan.

In Parliament, he has campaigned on a wide range of issues, including bus services, NHS dentistry and antisocial behaviour in line with the priorities he set out in his election campaign.

In October 2022, he was asked to join the Shadow front bench, as a Shadow Transport Minister, which includes responsibility for buses.

He is a member of the APPG for Rugby League and a proud Wakefield Trinity fan.

Prior to being elected, Simon was a proud NHS worker and was previously a Labour councillor and cabinet member for public health.

He studied theatre acting at Bretton Hall College in Wakefield.

Simon lives in Wakefield with his husband and their two young children.

Rt Hon Valerie Vaz MP was elected MP for Walsall South in May 2010 and re-elected in May 2015; June 2017 and December 2019. Valerie was appointed as Shadow Leader of the House (October 2016 - May 2021). Valerie is a member of USDAW.

Valerie is a solicitor and in Parliament has served on the Health Select Committee 2010-15, Regulatory Reform Committee 2010-15 and House of Commons Governance Committee 2014-15; After the 2015 election Valerie served on the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs 2016, Science & Technology 2015-16 Select Committees and appointed by The Speaker to the Panel of Chairs June 2015-16. Valerie is currently a member of the UK-EU Parliamentary Partnership and NATO Parliamentary Assembly. While in Parliament Valerie has published reports on Obesity and Diabetes Programmes in England: Capturing the State of Play in July 2011, 0845 telephone numbers; Instruments on Planes and a Glossary of Climate Change.

Before becoming an MP, Valerie was a Councillor in the London Borough of Ealing from 1986-90 and contested Twickenham in 1987 and the European Elections in 1999 (East Midlands List).

In October 2019 Valerie was appointed a member of HM Most Honourable Privy Council and received a Hon Doctor of Laws from the University of West London.

My track record as our local MP shows I know how to make change happen. In 14 years, I've personally helped thousands of local people. Whether taking on payday lenders, fighting for women's rights, helping widows or tackling rogue landlords, I've fought for a better future for everyone in Walthamstow. I ask for your vote so I can continue to champion our community and our causes.

Warrington South is my home. It's where I live and where I'm raising my family.

I care very deeply about Warrington and all our communities. As a local councillor and Cabinet Member for Children, I've spent years working alongside local residents, businesses, schools, charities and others to deliver for our town.

Warrington is a great place to live but not everyone has a fair chance to succeed; not only to survive, but to thrive. In Warrington South we're stuck without a voice in Westminster. Saddled instead with a Tory 'yes man' who delivers nothing but claims credit for everything.

Times are tough right now. The Tory cost of living is biting hard. Public services have been stripped to the bone. Wages are not keeping up with inflation. Our NHS is undergoing managed decline. The Tories have damaged our country. Hurt our communities. Neglected our region.

But we're fighting back. In Warrington South we're building a united, people-powered campaign - to return a Labour MP to Westminster and a Labour Government to Downing Street - so that we can finally get the change we so desperately need.

Get in touch and get involved. Together, we'll take the fight to the Tories and we will win Warrington South for Labour.

It is an honour to represent Washington and Sunderland West constituency as your Labour Party Member of Parliament (MP) in the House of Commons.

Alongside our Labour Councillors, I work hard to ensure that everyone in our area has access to the support and help they need.

Whether it is helping constituents when the benefits system has let them down; supporting local businesses or backing local campaigns, like the campaign against a gasification plant being built in Hillthorn Park, I always act with the best interests of everyone in Washington and Sunderland West in mind.

The Labour Party has not been in government since 2010. Since then, we've seen successive Conservative Governments devastate the economy, our region and household incomes.

This has only been made worse by poor choices from the Tories who have overseen the mismanagement of the Brexit deal, consistently acted against the interest of the country throughout the Coronavirus pandemic, and now during the devastating and spiralling cost of living crisis, are unable to get a grip on the economy and are unwilling to help those who most need it.

I will continue to hold this Conservative Government to account, to protect and improve your livelihoods and our local communities, trying to ensure nobody is left behind.

Labour's priorities will be the priorities of the British people: that starts with economic growth to provide the security our country needs to then rebuild Britain, so that it is the best country to grow up in, and the best to grow old in.

Matt has lived in Watford since 2011 and was elected to the council in 2012. In 2015, Matt was Labour's candidate for Watford in the general election and took Labour from third place to second. He currently works in health and social care and previously worked at the BBC.

I am Norfolk born and bred, and still live here with my fiancée and two primary school age children. I was one of the first in my family to go to university, at UEA; I am Leader of the Green Party; I’ve been a senior lecturer; and for the last decade, a national charity chief executive. I am standing, not to gain power, but because I care deeply about this area and improving people’s lives. I will do what’s right for constituents and won’t be told how to act and vote by a party. 

After 14 years of Conservative government, nothing seems to work and public services are being hollowed out. I won’t over-promise what I can achieve as an individual MP. But I can promise that I will campaign - inside and out of Parliament - to restore our public services, to ensure everyone can once more see an NHS dentist and make GP appointments, to build more affordable housing, to clean up our rivers, to invest in sustainable flood protection and to make life better for our communities.

Waveney Valley is one of the party's top target seats at this General Election. In the 2023 elections, Greens got the most votes across this whole area, with the Conservatives second and other parties a long way behind.

I’m Katie Lam, your Conservative candidate for the Weald of Kent. I live in Sissinghurst, in the heart of the Weald. I went to a comprehensive school and then Cambridge University. I’ve spent most of my career in finance, and I’ve worked in government securing investment for Britain and helping MI5 tackle terrorism. I’ve also been a governor of a school for deaf children for the last eight years — and I write scripts and lyrics for musicals!

My great-great-grandfather, Paul, was a German politician and fierce critic of the Nazis. When Hitler came to power, the whole family was persecuted. I grew up listening to my grandparents tell the story of that terrible time, so since I was a small child I’ve known what politics can do — for good and for bad — and always wanted to follow Paul into a life of elected public service.

If you send me to Westminster, I will fight relentlessly for what I believe in, what matters most to our rural way of life, and what matters most to you. I will fight for our farmers, for investment in our roads, to smash crime and anti-social behaviour and to crack down on illegal migration. I will demand upgrades to our health system, fight overdevelopment, help build first-class armed forces and to build a stronger economy free from unnecessary bureaucracy.

"I have worked tirelessly in my 101 days as your MP. We have had 14 long years of chaos and decline under the Tory government, I am pleased the country now has the opportunity to vote for change.

Keir Starmer has set out the six first steps the Labour party would take to turn things around and get Britain back on its feet.

I am regularly out on the doorstep talking to voters and I hear first hand how working people are struggling with the cost of living, how they can't get a doctor or dentist appointment… Families are worried about the education their children are receiving and local residents tell me they are sick of the antisocial behaviour they have to put up with day in, day out.

I was honoured to be elected as MP for Wellingborough and Rushden in February. In my 101 days, I have made real progress in laying my first steps for change and I hope the community will continue to place their trust in me to continue delivering the pledges I was elected on."

MY PLEDGES TO YOU and what I have done so far:

BANG THE DRUM FOR OUR TOWN CENTRES I have championed small businesses across the area and I have begun setting up a task force to bring key stakeholders from the town centres together.

WORK TO GET KNIVES OFF OUR STREETS I hosted an event in parliament with the charity Off The Streets to get knives off our streets. I will also work with the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner Danielle Stone closely on the issue.

HELP FIX OUR NHS I have organised a roundtable with local GP and dental surgeries and launched a parliament petition to call for an emergency care unit at Isebrook hospital. On the last PMQs, I asked the prime minister about the lack of dentists.

SORT THE POTHOLES! A road contract expert and I have been analysing the council and contractors processes to build a case. I have also met with the leader of the Conservative Council where we discussed the state of the roads, to apply pressure. 

PUT MORE MONEY BACK IN YOUR POCKET A Labour government will bring economic stability with tough spending rules to grow economy and keep taxes inflation and mortgages as low as possible.

I am running to be the Labour MP for Welwyn Hatfield, to serve the community that I call home. I was born in Welwyn Garden City and live in the constituency with my young family.

I live my Labour values through my work in social housing, as a supporter of local and national charities and time spent as a trustee of a credit union.

After thirteen years of a Conservative government and eighteen with Grant Shapps as the MP, our constituency is growing more unequal. There is a 10 year gap in life expectancy between people living in the centre of Hatfield and Welwyn Village, despite being just a few miles apart.

Our towns and villages have a proud history and vibrant community spirit, but people have been let down too often by the Conservatives. They deserve better.

As a local candidate with national experience, I am ready to take on Grant Shapps and believe we can secure a historic Labour gain in Welwyn Hatfield at the next General Election.

I'm proud to be our Labour candidate for the new West Bromwich constituency which covers Great Barr, Yew Tree, West Brom, Oldbury, Rowley and Tividale.

I live in West Bromwich and I've already got a track record of making a difference for our community. Last year I led the campaign that saved the 45 bus that so many local people rely on, and I was also part of the group that saved some children's football pitches from being closed.

At weekends you can find me out jogging in Sandwell Valley or knocking on doors listening to people.

If you've got a question, or an idea to support the area, then please get in touch.

After 14 years of Tory failure, and 18 years of an out-of-touch MP , I pledge to you a different style of politics. Weston will always be my top priority and I will only promise what I can deliver.



I'm out on the doors, speaking with voters every day and I will be as accessible and engaged as possible, it's about time Weston got the representation we deserve.



Feel free to get in touch with any questions - or if you'd like to help us campaign locally to win here for the first time, get Labour into government, and change lives.

While you consider how you plan to cast your vote, I would like you to think about how you would feel waking up on the morning of July 5th and the Labour Party has gained a significant majority? It may be that you are a committed Socialist who wants to pay higher taxes, grant an amnesty to illegal immigrants, build on our precious green space and declare a war on motorists. But as someone who has had the privilege of representing West Worcestershire in Parliament for 14 years, I don't sense an appetite for Socialism on the doorsteps. I am hearing that voters want us to stick to our plan and deliver on the priorities that matter most to us all. The pandemic and Putin's energy crisis have meant a tough time for everyone but the economy has bounced back and inflation is now down to target.

Alec has lived within the proposed Wetherby & Easingwold constituency for over 25 years and is regularly out and about campaigning across the area and meeting fellow residents. 

The son of two teachers, Alec was born in 1976 and educated at his local comprehensive school. He studied mechanical engineering at Brunel University where he graduated with honours in 1998. After graduation, Alec joined the Royal Navy before moving to Yorkshire where he managed the Nanotechnology Facility at the University of Leeds.

Alec has served as the Member of Parliament for the Wetherby area since 2010, winning the Elmet & Rothwell constituency from Labour. Alec's working week is usually spent in the House of Commons Monday to Thursday, before he returns home to hold a mixture of one-to-one advice surgeries, supermarket surgeries and street surgeries on Fridays and Saturdays. Alec is regularly out and about campaigning across the revised Wetherby & Easingwold listening to the views of voters. 

Alec has been a committed constituency Member of Parliament and has driven forward a mission to make his constituency dementia friendly, including the publication of his Dementia Directory. Improving dementia services is a personal commitment for Alec and he is already planning the expansion of his Dementia Strategy into Boroughbridge, Easingwold, Tadcaster and surrounding villages.

His constituents describe Alec as someone who gets things done, whether it's supporting local charities, securing victory for a ten year campaign to fund new disabled-access at a local railway station, or delivering funds to rebuild four local schools.

Alec is a former Minister of State for Defence and was in charge of military procurement. During his time in Parliament, Alec has served as a Chairman of the All Party Parliamentary Group for Thalidomide and, in conjunction with the Thalidomide Trust, secured the extension of an £80m Thalidomide health grant to support the independent living of victims of the Thalidomide drug. In Parliament, he has also secured Adjournment Debates to raise matters associated with dementia care, welfare support and sentencing for drink-driving offences. He is a champion for workers’ rights and introduced the National Minimum Wage (Workplace Internships) Bill to the House of Commons, calling for the abolition of unpaid internships. Alec has led a series of debates on women's health, calling for further awareness of Endometriosis and better support for patients injured during pelvic mesh surgery.

Alec takes a keen interest in foreign affairs. After a period serving as a Parliamentary Private Secretary in the Foreign & Commonwealth Office between 2014 and 2015, former Prime Minister David Cameron appointed Alec as a UK representative to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in December 2015. Since then, Alec has concentrated on defence and security matters within the alliance and was appointed Leader of the UK Delegation in 2020.

Alec has represented the United Kingdom at a number of Rose Roth seminars, bringing together NATO partner countries. He also took part in election monitoring in Georgia’s 2016 General Election.

Alec is a former Vice-Chairman (International) of the Conservative Party, a role which involved building relationships with international sister parties and working with the Westminster Foundation for Democracy to enhance democratic institutions and political party structures in the developing world.

Alec is a Formula 1 enthusiast and is a former Deputy Chairman of the All Party Parliamentary Group for Formula 1, so he enjoys spending a few hours watching the Grand Prix on a Sunday.

Cumbria is my home and I'm so proud to be standing to be your Labour MP and Whitehaven and Workington's voice in Parliament.



I live here in Cumbria with my partner and our two Lurchers, Huck and Molly, and I'm also a volunteer in the Mountain Rescue in the Lake District, a challenging role which I love.



West Cumbria has a proud history of shaping the UK's future and we can again. Our biggest problems all have answers here. But we've been stuck on the wrong path for years thanks to the Tories, who've failed to deliver for our area, crashed the economy and left thousands of local families struggling to make ends meet and worried for the future.



I have a record of delivery outside politics that shows you can have confidence in me to get the job done as your MP. My whole career has been spent delivering change for those left out or forgotten. Whether as a teacher working in tough schools, founding and leading a national charity which recruited thousands more social workers, or leading a landmark national review for vulnerable children which delivered £200 million of new investment to support children and families.



As your MP I will fight for and deliver for West Cumbria. I'll be spending the next few months meeting thousands of local people, listening to your concerns and turning those into my priorities to deliver as your MP after the next General Election.

Lisa Nandy is the Labour candidate for Wigan and the shadow Cabinet Minister for International Development. Since being elected, Nandy has pursued wide-ranging campaigns – from child abuse, educational allowance, regional development, housing, and against human rights abuses in Palestine. Following her initial election in 2010 Lisa has been re-elected to Parliament three times.

Lisa was born in Manchester to Luise and Dipak Nandy, a Indian-born activist and academic who was integral to drafting the 1976 Race Relations Act.  Lisa was educated at Parrs Wood High School and Holy Cross College before studying politics at Newcastle University and public policy at Birkbeck, University of London. She then worked as an aide to Walthamstow MP Neil Gerrard, a researcher for homelessness charity Centrepoint and a senior policy adviser at The Children’s Society.

Nandy was Parliamentary Private Secretary to Tessa Jowell from 2010 to 2012, Shadow Minister for Children from 2012 to 2013, and Shadow Minister for Charities and Civil Society from 2012 to 2015, with responsibility for Labour Policy on the voluntary sector. She served as Shadow Secretary of State for Energy and Climate Change from 2015, shadowing Amber Rudd.

A key focus of Lisa’s work in Parliament has been raising the issue of towns, which have often been overlooked in the discussions on regional development and devolution. As co-founder of the Centre for Towns she spearheaded the campaign for Labour to represent and champion the coastal and industrial towns which are the bedrock of the Labour movement. These areas deserve a Labour government to breathe new life in to their regional economies and to give them the power to make their own decisions.

After a further four years as a backbench MP, Lisa stood as a candidate in the 2020 Labour Party leadership election. She was subsequently appointed Shadow Foreign Secretary in April 2020. From November 2021 to 2023, Lisa served as Shadow Secretary of State for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities – shadowing Michael Gove and holding the government to account on their flagship policy while demonstrating Labour’s commitment to homeownership, housebuilding and tackling regional inequality.

Lisa has been in her current role as Shadow Cabinet Minister for International Development since November 2023, working to outline and highlight Labour’s commitment to champion Britain’s generosity and support for some of the world’s most disadvantaged.

Brought up in Birkenhead, Matthew has been an active campaigner across the Wirral for over a decade. Whilst a Councillor for the Woodchurch, he worked to establish resident groups, secure opportunities for young people and get the first playground in a generation built.

He is passionate about expanding opportunities for everyone, protecting our beautiful environment and restoring public services. He believes in a strong economy and wants to support local businesses who do so much to help Wirral grow.

Fighting to fix our local NHS: - Clive Jones has made safeguarding our local NHS his top priority. It's personal for Clive because he relied on local health services when he was diagnosed with cancer 15 years ago. 

Tackling the cost of living: As leader of Wokingham Borough he helped deliver real action to support those in need, providing free school meals during holidays, helping people directly with £150,000 in funding for those most at risk, and opening warm spaces through the winter. 

Protecting our environment: Clive Jones is fighting to make sure water companies clean up our rivers.

I will be a hard-working, full-time MP for Wokingham, fighting for a fair deal for Wokingham residents and prioritising the issues that you have told me matter most: fixing the NHS, tackling the cost-of-living crisis and stopping the dumping of sewage in our rivers.

I am truly honoured to be selected as the Labour Party parliamentary candidate for Wolverhampton & Willenhall.



I grew up in Baylis Avenue, Ashmore Park. I went to Danesmore Primary and Wednesfield High school. I studied Biochemistry at The University of Wolverhampton. And I raised my family here.

I'm a Deputy Headteacher. I'm not a career politician, I'm a teacher. But I can't stand by any longer. I'm standing to make real change.



I am shaped by the experiences of seeing my parents and community work incredibly hard for little reward. As a Deputy Headteacher, I am seeing more and more families having to work around these anti-family hours just to make ends meet and it's still not enough.



Wolverhampton & Willenhall has much to be proud of but we are being hindered by the Conservative governments chaos and incompetence. People are paying much more tax whilst getting so little in return. People struggling to get a GP appointment, record A&E waiting times, record NHS waiting lists for treatment, a housing and social care crisis, and pay restraint for many years leading to industrial disputes.

We need to fix the economy to grow the economy. Wolverhampton & Willenhall can make more, sell more and achieve more; we have the skills, expertise and workforce. I will work hand in hand with the City council to attract further investment and continue building ambitious projects.



I will fight for the people of Wolverhampton North East to raise living standards for everyone and not just the privileged few. I will work tirelessly for a better, fairer future for all in Wolverhampton & Willenhall.

Worcester is my home and over the past 17 years I've built my life and family here.

Our city could be thriving, but it's been let down by a government lacking vision. Our roads and busses, our healthcare and hospital are failing under the Conservatives' neglect. Our schools are in crisis and local businesses are closing.

Meanwhile we face climate breakdown, a global emergency, and the realities of daily life make change seem impossible.

I'm standing because I believe there's hope.

I've dedicated my business career to building the green economy by decarbonising heat. I head Bosch's innovation team developing hydrogen-ready boilers, and I am an industry leader in hydrogen and zero-carbon heat. I speak publicly at various conferences informing the Westminster energy debate.

As a City Councillor, I tackled the climate crisis head on, pushing for higher local ambition to insulate buildings and develop strategy for safe streets to walk and cycle. I fought for outdoor play for children. I know the tough reality of life for many in Worcester and through casework I've made a difference.

We can transform lives and build a sustainable economy, by putting people at the centre of our politics and economy.

I stepped up because I want to see integrity and leadership in politics. I'm part of this city - I use our local services and my children go to local schools. I have built and led teams, and brought change in business, industry and national policy.

I'm ready to be what Worcester deserves - a present, truly local MP with a vision for our city, and an effective voice in Westminster.

statement_to_voters:
First elected in 2015, Rachael campaigns tirelessly for her constituents in York Central. With a career in the NHS, working as a senior physiotherapist in ITU and acute medicine and as the Head of Health at Unite, Rachael continues to use her expertise in Westminster to progress healthcare and protect the NHS and is Vice Chair of the Health and Social Care Health Select Committee.



With the challenges people experience in York, Rachael has recently advanced legislation to regulate Short Term Holiday Lets, and speaks regularly on issues from housing and development, the economy, health and social care and the environment and climate. As a trade unionist, she also makes the case for advancing workers' rights, not least through her Bill to tackle Bullying at Work.



Central to Rachael's work, is listening to the issues that constituents raise and bringing their voice to Parliament, especially the inequality and injustices that so many have faced under the Tories. Not only does she work across agencies in York to enhance services and support businesses, but takes up the issues residents need addressing.

Luke is Labour's Parliamentary Candidate in the target seat of York Outer. Luke is a new dad to baby Robin and husband to Bethany. He was born in York, went to Huntington School, and has lived all across the constituency in Haxby, Strensall, Heworth, and Osbaldwick.

Having studied economics and politics at university, Luke went onto the Bank of England where he worked on the project to launch the new polymer banknotes. Luke then became a regulator at the Financial Conduct Authority where he worked on projects to protect vulnerable customers and reduce fraud.

Luke is presently leads counter-fraud work for a global tech company.

Luke previously stood for York Outer in 2017, coming a strong second by securing over 21,000 votes.
